prs.title: Handle multidimensional categorical action spaces
prs.head: e9d04af53b8e3d2ec98b25d1436d602e7f52491a
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem and change

Fixes #503.

Torch `MultiCategoricalMixin.act()` passes `MultiDiscrete.nvec.tolist()` directly to `torch.split`. A multidimensional `nvec` produces nested lists, so both logits and probabilities policies raise before sampling an action.

Flatten the category counts in both distribution-construction paths. The output keeps the existing flattened action convention, while one-dimensional spaces keep their current behavior.

## Validation

The new regression uses the public model instantiator with `MultiDiscrete([[2, 3], [4, 5]])`. Both logits and probabilities cases check action shape and bounds, uniform joint log probability and entropy against `log(120)`, and finite, nonzero policy gradients.

- [Unchanged-source baseline](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43817142988/job/133131673269): **2 failed, 45 passed**; both new cases fail in `torch.split`.
- [Fixed validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43817359163): the complete model-instantiator directory has **47 passed** on Linux/Python 3.10/Torch 1.11 and Linux/Windows/Python 3.13/Torch 2.15. All three utils jobs pass, including the existing spaces, framework and distributed tests. The complete Torch workflow also passes all nine jobs.
- The complete configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43817359116) pass. The regression itself runs on CPU.

This change is independent of #481's occupied-space sizing. It only changes categorical head splitting and its regression; it does not include the existing space-sizing patch.

prs.title: Preserve zero probabilities when sampling JAX actions
prs.head: a2303b210f0ed06575a4fd64c72e1cbd317aa5bc
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem and change

Fixes #505.

JAX categorical policies clamp normalized probabilities to epsilon before converting them to logits. Using those clamped logits for sampling assigns positive weight to actions whose policy probability is zero, so a probability mask no longer excludes those actions. This is especially visible with bfloat16 outputs.

Use logits from the actual normalized probabilities for sampling in both categorical and multicategorical policies. Keep the existing clamped log-density path unchanged, and keep the existing logits-input sampling path unchanged.

## Validation

Four CPU regression/control cases exercise the public JAX model instantiators with one supported action per categorical head, a fixed key and 1,024 observations. They cover categorical/multicategorical policies and probability/logit inputs.

- [Unchanged-source baseline](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43819603241/job/133139390112): **2 failed, 21 passed**. The probability cases sample 44 excluded categorical actions and 93 excluded multicategorical head selections; both logits controls pass.
- [Fixed validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43820098052): the complete model-instantiator directory has **23 passed** on JAX 0.4.31 and 0.12.0.1. Both utils jobs pass, including spaces, framework and distributed tests. Every sampled action is in the original support, and returned log probabilities remain finite.
- The full configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43820098061) pass. The remaining components jobs in the existing workflow were still running when this validation summary was prepared.

This change concerns sampling support. It does not change the separate entropy or per-head random-key handling.

prs.title: Parse nested operations in generated model expressions
prs.head: 68b32143c7f7346ecca17101b2be72495d4f9088
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #507

## Problem and change

The input and output AST visitors translate the outer function call but do not visit calls inside its arguments. Documented combinations such as nested concatenation or an output activation around concatenation consequently produce undefined names in generated models.

Visit child nodes before translating each call, in the Torch, JAX and Warp input/output visitors. This adds one recursive traversal call to each visitor and preserves the existing top-level mappings.

## Validation

Six regressions instantiate and evaluate actual deterministic models, covering nested input and output expressions in all three backends. The expected tensors are calculated independently with direct Torch/NumPy operations.

- Unchanged source: [Torch](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43818465209/job/133135894726) **2 failed, 45 passed**; [JAX](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43818465223/job/133135883724) **2 failed, 19 passed**; [Warp](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43818467958/job/133135799208) **2 failed, 18 passed**. All six new cases fail with an unresolved `concatenate`.
- Fixed source: the complete Torch model-instantiator directory has **47 passed** across its minimum and latest Linux/Windows matrix; the JAX directory has **21 passed** on minimum and latest dependencies. Their utils jobs pass.
- Both [Warp utils jobs](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43818797914) pass, with **20 passed** in the complete model-instantiator directory on minimum/latest dependencies. The complete [Torch](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43818798017), [JAX](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43818797905) and Warp workflows pass, including agents, multi-agents, trainers, environments and utils.
- The repository-wide [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43818797863) pass. The new cases run on CPU.

The source change is six traversal calls across three files; the other three changed files contain the regression cases.

## Related history

#432 was fixed by #433, merged on 2026-09-10. That change added an `else` so a top-level `concatenate` does not fall through to an activation lookup on an `ast.Attribute`; it is already present in the tested base. The failure here occurs when an operation is nested inside another call: child calls are not visited, so generated input/output code retains an undefined inner `concatenate`. The new regressions reproduce this distinct runtime failure on the current base.

prs.title: Train CEM policies with elite action log likelihoods
prs.head: c76257923bb6eb13335c85d4ae99235dbddbf3b3
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #509

## Problem and change

CEM treats the policy's raw `net_output` as logits for one categorical distribution. Probability-output policies therefore optimize the wrong objective, and the documented multicategorical policies cannot complete an update: PyTorch flattens their action heads and JAX reads the nonexistent `MultiDiscrete.n` attribute.

Compute the negative mean log likelihood of the recorded elite actions through the policy's existing `taken_actions` interface in both backends. This uses the policy's configured normalization and joint categorical distribution while preserving the ordinary categorical-logit objective.

## Validation

The new tests exercise actual two-step rollouts and optimizer updates with categorical and multicategorical policies, each configured for probabilities or logits. They check the analytical losses `log(1.5)` and `log(3)`, finite parameter updates, and the analytical PyTorch bias gradients.

- Unchanged-source baselines: [PyTorch](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43818799512/job/133136847253) has **3 failed, 53 passed, 52 skipped**; [JAX](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43818799540/job/133136847164) has **3 failed, 23 passed, 22 skipped**. The existing categorical-logit controls pass.
- The fixed [PyTorch workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43819971939) passes all **9 jobs**, including minimum dependencies and latest Linux/Windows dependencies. The minimum-dependency agents directory has **56 passed, 52 skipped**.
- The fixed [JAX workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43819972137) passes all **6 jobs**. Both minimum/latest dependency jobs report **26 passed, 22 skipped** for agents, **6 passed, 6 skipped** for multi-agents, and **16 passed, 22 skipped** for trainers.
- All configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43819971949) pass.

The regression uses one environment and one completed episode. Episode selection and discounting are unchanged.

prs.title: Use absolute Optax learning rates across JAX agents
prs.head: 8a4a585007db02813d55a9975a8738e249c31f92
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #511.

## Problem and change

Optax schedules return absolute learning-rate values. Multiplying those values into the previous rate causes schedules such as the documented `constant_schedule(value=1e-4)` to collapse the learning rate on every call.

Assign ordinary schedule results directly across all 11 JAX agent and multi-agent implementations. Preserve KL-adaptive updates, the configured rate before the first scheduler call, and the existing call timing/timestep argument.

## Validation

The regressions run the actual agents. Constant-schedule assertions cover A2C, CEM, DDPG, DDQN, DQN, PPO, RPO, SAC, TD3, IPPO and MAPPO. A focused CEM rollout also checks three successive constant/linear schedule values, no-scheduler and KL-adaptive controls, finite parameter changes, and the logged learning rates.

- On unchanged source, both [minimum](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43822419700/job/133148333796) and [latest](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43822419700/job/133148334161) JAX agents jobs report **22 failed, 4 passed, 22 skipped**. The constant schedule returns `1e-4`, but the first stored rate is `2e-7`.
- With the fix, the complete [JAX workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43823132086) passes all **6 jobs**. Both dependency versions report **26 passed, 22 skipped** for agents, **6 passed, 6 skipped** for multi-agents, and **16 passed, 22 skipped** for trainers.
- All configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43823132015) pass.
- Existing Hypothesis settings and training budgets are unchanged.

This corrects the schedule-value interpretation introduced in #245 and #255 while retaining the KL schedule detection from #401.

prs.title: Detach persistent scaler statistics after differentiable forwards
prs.head: 4bfaa9639bfe154fdd372c63f51db4ea1306ac08
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #513.

## Problem and change

With `train=True, no_grad=False`, `RunningStandardScaler` stores the current input’s autograd graph in its running mean and variance. The next independent encoder batch traverses the already-freed graph and raises during backward.

Detach the persistent statistics after computing the current output. This preserves the current batch’s derivatives through the normalization statistics while preventing earlier batches from becoming part of later training graphs.

## Validation

The regression trains a real `Linear -> RunningStandardScaler -> loss -> SGD` pipeline for three independent batches. Each output and encoder gradient is compared with a fresh scaler loaded from the previous detached statistics. It covers 2-D and 3-D batches, forward and inverse transforms, finite parameter updates, and the default no-gradient mode.

- On unchanged source, the [minimum](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43825155413/job/133157130440), [latest Linux](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43825155413/job/133157130531), and [latest Windows](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43825155413/job/133157130387) agents jobs each report **4 failed, 53 passed, 52 skipped**. All four differentiable cases fail on the second independent batch with the freed-graph error; the no-gradient control passes.
- The fixed [PyTorch workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43825768783) passes all **9 jobs**. All three dependency/platform component jobs report **57 passed, 52 skipped** for agents, **15 passed, 15 skipped** for multi-agents, and **20 passed, 34 skipped** for trainers.
- All configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43825768790) pass.

The moment calculations, saved-state layout and current-batch gradient values are unchanged.

prs.title: Advance PRNG keys outside compiled JAX policy updates
prs.head: 36c64229a322f91ba1d60cfd20e86a2c0aeeb22e
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem and change

Fixes #515.

JAX stochastic policy mixins advance Python counters inside `act`. When an algorithm calls `act` from a compiled policy-loss function, those increments execute during tracing and the compiled computation reuses the same sampling key on later gradient updates. SAC consequently reuses its policy noise even when it performs several updates.

Allow the Gaussian, categorical and multicategorical mixins to honor an explicit `inputs["key"]`. Advance agent-owned keys outside the compiled policy updates in A2C, CEM, PPO, RPO, SAC, IPPO and MAPPO, and pass each subkey into the policy inputs. Ordinary calls without an explicit key continue to advance the model's own sampling sequence.

## Validation

A regression runs three actual SAC gradient updates with fixed model parameters (`learning_rate=0`) and identical replay inputs, while observing the original compiled policy update's log probabilities. It compares successive update batches without replacing the loss computation.

- On unchanged source, both [minimum](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43823551413/job/133151940075) and [latest](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43823551413/job/133151940228) JAX agents jobs report **1 failed, 22 passed, 22 skipped**. The second and third update batches are identical.
- With the fix, the full [JAX workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43825117675) passes all **6 jobs**. Both dependency versions report **23 passed, 22 skipped** for agents, **6 passed, 6 skipped** for multi-agents, and **16 passed, 22 skipped** for trainers.
- The model-instantiator directory has **22 passing tests** on both dependency versions. Added controls cover all three stochastic mixins: an explicit key replays the same result under `jax.jit`, a different key changes the samples, and implicit sampling still advances when the caller reuses one input dictionary.
- All configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43825117726) pass.

This changes policy-update key handling; it does not alter the categorical-head sampling split or entropy formulas.

prs.title: Support scalar parameter leaves in JAX gradient reduction
prs.head: e579e0523708450c450583cf374ffb8014d3aa95
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem and change

Fixes #517.

JAX gradient reduction reconstructs every flattened parameter leaf using `leaf.at[:]`. A scalar leaf has no sliceable axis, so a scalar trainable parameter raises `IndexError` before its gradient can be applied.

Use ellipsis indexing when restoring the leaf. This supports scalar and nonscalar shapes while preserving the existing collective operation, tree structure and per-leaf dtype handling.

## Validation

The regression obtains gradients from a real Flax policy with a trainable scalar gain and dense parameters, reduces them through `Model.reduce_parameters`, and applies three finite SGD updates. Additional cases cover a scalar root, float16/float32 scalars in a nested mixed-shape tree, an empty array and an unchanged nonscalar control.

- On unchanged source, [minimum](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43826681451/job/133162067241) and [latest](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43826681451/job/133162067420) JAX each report **3 failed, 17 passed** in the distributed directory; all scalar cases fail with the zero-dimensional indexing error.
- The fixed [JAX workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43827306287) passes all **6 jobs**. Both dependency versions report **20 passed** in the distributed directory, **22 passed, 22 skipped** for agents, **6 passed, 6 skipped** for multi-agents, and **16 passed, 22 skipped** for trainers.
- All configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43827306364) pass.

The regression uses one local CPU device and validates the actual reduction and reconstruction path; it does not claim a cross-worker or GPU run.

prs.title: Use independent keys for JAX model and parameter initialization
prs.head: 68a083fd92389e62a004ec5b2ab3f906a983646b
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem and change

Fixes #519.

Default JAX model initialization reuses the global key, so separately created SAC/TD3 critics with identical architectures start with identical parameters. Random parameter reinitialization also reuses one key for all leaves and subsequent calls, making same-shaped layers identical.

Consume a fresh subkey for each default model initialization and each selected parameter initializer. An explicit `init_state_dict(key=...)` remains reproducible and does not consume the global key. Resetting the seed replays the default initialization sequence.

## Validation

The new model regressions check independent model outputs, seed replay, explicit-key replay without global-key consumption, independent random initialization of same-shaped layers, consecutive initializer calls, unchanged unselected parameters, and constant initializers. Existing SAC/TD3 training tests now assert that their initial twin critics differ.

- On unchanged source, [minimum](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43826034513/job/133159993043) and [latest](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43826034513/job/133159993047) model jobs each report **4 failed, 21 passed**.
- On unchanged source, [minimum](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43826034513/job/133159993351) and [latest](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43826034513/job/133159992676) agents jobs each report **4 failed, 18 passed, 22 skipped** from identical SAC/TD3 critic parameters.
- The fixed [JAX workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43827235828) passes all **6 jobs**. Both dependency versions report **25 passed** for models, **22 passed, 22 skipped** for agents, **6 passed, 6 skipped** for multi-agents, and **16 passed, 22 skipped** for trainers.
- All configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43827235796) pass.

This changes the default random initialization sequence. Explicit-key initialization remains the way to request identical parameter draws.

prs.title: Preserve complete JAX random keys during restoration and device changes
prs.head: 1318caf60921d7c653a107455686ac5d1fd95b35
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #521

## Problem and change

The JAX configuration reconstructs a NumPy PRNG key from only its second word, changing the random stream when restoring saved keys. Device assignment also converts existing keys through that path and fails for typed keys.

Keep numeric seeds distinct from full keys. Numeric seeds still use `jax.random.PRNGKey` with the configured implementation; full NumPy/JAX keys are transferred with `jax.device_put`, preserving all key data and typed-key information.

## Validation

- On unchanged source, [minimum](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43830937856/job/133175847830) and [latest](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43830937856/job/133175847800) JAX framework jobs each report **4 failed, 11 passed**.
- The fixed [JAX workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43831631026) passes all **6 jobs**. Both framework jobs report **15 passed**, covering Threefry/RBG host restoration, typed and legacy keys, device assignment, numeric seeds, and direct key assignment.
- The root configuration change also passes all **9 Torch jobs** and **6 Warp jobs** in their existing workflows: [Torch](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43831631110), [Warp](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43831630976).
- All configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43831630997) pass.

Tests use CPU device assignment and verify exact key data and generated samples.

prs.title: Use effective agent rollouts when sizing runner memory
prs.head: 34bdcee14b785849116c9c56aa617763efc800bc
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #523

## Problem and change

Automatic runner memory sizing reads `cfg["agent"]["rollouts"]` directly, so omitting the optional setting raises `KeyError` despite the agent dataclass defining a default.

Resolve the effective agent configuration before allocating memory in the Torch, JAX and Warp runners, and use its rollout count for automatic sizing. Reuse that resolved configuration when creating the agent.

## Validation

Each backend has three public Runner cases: default rollouts with automatic memory, an explicit rollout count, and an explicit memory size. Each case runs two PPO updates and checks finite changed policy weights, the selected memory size, and unchanged caller configuration.

- Unchanged-source [Torch](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43830228176/job/133173529279): **1 failed, 22 passed, 34 skipped** in trainers.
- Unchanged-source [Warp](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43830228111/job/133173529453): **1 failed, 12 passed, 12 skipped** in trainers.
- Fixed workflows: [Torch, 9 jobs](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43831079967), [JAX, 6 jobs](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43831079991), and [Warp, 6 jobs](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43831079968), all successful.
- Fixed trainer suites report **23 passed/34 skipped** (Torch minimum), **19 passed/22 skipped** (both JAX versions), and **13 passed/12 skipped** (Warp minimum).
- All configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43831080004) pass.

prs.title: Initialize the Warp Gaussian entropy reduction accumulator
prs.head: c1e2b1e2eac5b6ff6d052d0f1651239c4cba75c9
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #525

## Problem and change

The Gaussian entropy kernel sums into a scalar using `wp.atomic_add`, but `get_entropy` allocates that scalar with `wp.empty`. Reused nonzero or NaN allocation contents therefore corrupt the entropy used by the policy.

Allocate the reduction accumulator with `wp.zeros`.

## Validation

The regression uses a real generated Gaussian model, its `act` output, the production entropy kernel, and a real Warp Tape backward pass. It makes unspecified allocation contents deterministic by wrapping `wp.empty` during entropy allocation, covering zero, -17 and NaN contents with batch sizes 1 and 5. It checks the analytic entropy and the log-standard-deviation gradient.

- Unchanged-source [minimum](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43831932004/job/133179062897) and [latest](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43831932004/job/133179062892) model jobs each report **4 failed, 20 passed**.
- The fixed [Warp workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43833023526) passes all **6 jobs**. Both model jobs report **24 passed**; both framework suites report **220 passed**.
- All configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43833023408) pass.

Related: #434 introduced the sum reduction; #462 left the accumulator allocation unchanged.

prs.title: Preserve gradients from every Warp concatenation input
prs.head: 53b20f9f2c00f70c5baf8f2949f960578585b37c
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #527

## Problem and change

`concatenate` copies the first input's `requires_grad` flag to its output. Concatenating fixed observations before trainable features therefore detaches those features, even though later inputs require gradients.

Require output gradients when any input requires them. The copy and dtype behavior remain unchanged.

## Validation

Eight real Warp Tape cases cover batch sizes 1 and 3 and all four combinations of input gradient flags. They check output values, gradient ownership and the analytic mean gradient. Both inputs use the same float32 dtype, so the regression isolates concatenation from cast behavior.

- Unchanged-source [minimum](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43833220601/job/133183335088) and [latest](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43833220601/job/133183334378) jobs each report **2 failed, 226 passed**. The failures are the fixed-first/trainable-second cases.
- The fixed [Warp workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43834225080) passes all **6 jobs**; both framework suites report **228 passed**.
- All configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43834225407) pass.

Related: #394 added dtype handling to concatenation; it did not change which inputs determine gradient ownership.

prs.title: Preserve gradients through Warp floating dtype conversions
prs.head: 8d012b6eee54976125f0ff716b6d9ba6c81e4ac8
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #529

## Problem and change

`type_cast` propagates `requires_grad` to its result, but all four conversion kernels disable backward. A floating dtype conversion inside a differentiable computation therefore silently leaves its source gradient at zero.

Enable Warp's generated backward pass for the existing conversion kernels.

## Validation

Ten regression cases exercise all six conversions between float16, float32 and float64 across ranks 1–4 using real `wp.Tape` backward passes. Identity conversions and integer round trips provide value and ownership controls.

- Unchanged-source [minimum](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43832948585/job/133182433781) and [latest](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43832948585/job/133182433716) framework jobs each report **6 failed, 224 passed**. All floating conversion paths return zero source gradients.
- The fixed [Warp workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43834218091) passes all **6 jobs**; both framework suites report **230 passed**.
- All configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43834218070) pass.

Related: #394 added dtype conversion to concatenation; it did not enable the cast kernels' backward passes.

prs.title: Stabilize Warp sigmoid and softplus values and derivatives
prs.head: 4f974dade0761c2fc2921354e457f61139d207cc
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #531

## Problem and change

The public Warp sigmoid and softplus utilities evaluate unbounded exponentials. Large finite inputs can produce infinite softplus values and nonfinite backward gradients.

Use sign-dependent equivalent formulas whose exponentials have nonpositive arguments. Evaluate float16 intermediates in float32 before casting the result back. Existing float16 value tests now use a float64 mathematical reference with their original tolerances.

## Validation

Twelve regression cases check inputs from -1000 to 1000 for float16, float32 and float64. Forward checks cover ranks 1–4 and both allocation modes; backward checks use a real Warp Tape and analytic derivatives.

- Unchanged-source [minimum](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43831553791/job/133177843638) and [latest](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43831553791/job/133177844164) framework jobs each report **9 failed, 223 passed**.
- The fixed [Warp workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43834784765) passes all **6 jobs**. Both framework suites report **232 passed**, including the existing moderate-value cases.
- All configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43834784315) pass.

This change concerns `skrl.utils.framework.warp` activation utilities.

prs.title: Save and restore live JAX optimizer checkpoint state
prs.head: abe2d2043fa4a05af1f870a173df5ffdd6916556
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #533

## Problem and change

JAX optimizers are immutable PyTrees. Training replaces the active optimizer after every update, but `checkpoint_modules` still holds its original object. Manual, periodic and best checkpoints consequently serialize stale moments. Single-agent loading ignores optimizer PyTrees, and multi-agent loading rejects JAX state-dict modules.

Resolve registered immutable optimizers from their active attributes when collecting checkpoint values. Restore their serialized PyTrees on the agent device and reconnect active attributes. Load multi-agent JAX model and preprocessor parameters through their existing `state_dict` representation.

## Validation

The regression trains CEM for three episodes, saves/restores it and checks both optimizer moments and the next actual training update. It also checks combined/separate periodic and best checkpoints, legacy model-only loading, and two-agent IPPO model/preprocessor/moment restoration followed by another update on an identical rollout with controlled sampling.

- The refined unchanged-source [latest JAX baseline](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43829808081/job/133172143685) reports **4 failed, 23 passed, 22 skipped**: CEM snapshots retain step zero, and IPPO loading raises `NotImplementedError`.

- All configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43832838666) pass.

Replay contents and random state are supplied by the continuation test; this change restores registered checkpoint modules and does not add replay or RNG checkpointing. Related #354 concerns the Torch `skip_modules` option.

prs.title: Compute differentiable Warp Gaussian product reductions
prs.head: dfad8033897b9ac4bde0f4b0aee4f1b697f18156
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #535

## Problem and change

Warp `GaussianMixin` accepts the documented `reduction="prod"`, but both sampled-action and provided-action kernels leave that branch empty. The returned log probabilities are therefore zeros.

Compute the component log densities, then multiply them using differentiable pairwise kernels. The reduction supports odd action counts and factors near zero without dividing by a component.

## Validation

Twenty-five regression cases cover all four reduction modes, action counts 1, 3 and 4, sampled and provided actions, plus a near-zero factor. Real Warp Tape checks compare product gradients against analytic mean and log-standard-deviation derivatives.

- Unchanged-source [minimum](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43833493228/job/133184275742) and [latest](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43833493228/job/133184276090) model jobs each report **7 failed, 36 passed**. Other reductions pass their controls.
- The fixed [Warp workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43834709447) passes all **6 jobs**; both model suites report **43 passed**.
- All configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43834709437) pass.

Related: #375 introduced the Warp model; #434 and #462 changed other Gaussian calculations while leaving product reduction unimplemented.

prs.title: Support Warp Polyak updates for every parameter rank
prs.head: f9c03c75932bdcb7e5ce1d1440934b2f18b1765c
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #537

## Problem and change

Warp model soft updates launch a kernel declared for two-dimensional float32 arrays. The built-in Gaussian model contains a one-dimensional `log_std` parameter, so a soft target update fails. Custom floating parameters with other ranks or dtypes fail for the same reason.

Dispatch generic in-place Polyak kernels for ranks 1–4 and pass the coefficient in each parameter's dtype.

## Validation

Forty regression cases cover float16/32/64 parameters at ranks 1–4 with coefficients 0, 0.25 and 1, plus four coefficients on an actual generated Gaussian model. They verify the weighted result, unchanged source values and preserved destination storage.

- The unchanged-source [first](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43834432854/job/133187436789) and [second](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43834432854/job/133187437064) Warp model jobs each report **25 failed, 33 passed**, including the built-in Gaussian vector parameter.
- The fixed [Warp workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43836538506) passes all **6 jobs**. Both model suites report **58 passed**.
- All configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43836538521) pass.

Related: #375 introduced the Warp model; #422 migrated it to warp-nn while retaining the specialized averaging kernel.

prs.title: Propagate parallel trainer worker errors and clean up processes
prs.head: 26a1743f5c67fcef1f1b16f2a8ce5049e5fb9d4c
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #539

## Problem and change

A Python exception in a parallel trainer worker exits that process without releasing the parent's barrier. Training or evaluation then hangs. A parent-side environment exception also leaves the worker processes alive.

Send worker tracebacks back through the pipes and abort the barrier on failure. Wrap both multi-process train/eval paths in managed cleanup that reaps workers and closes pipes and queues, including when the parent raises.

## Validation

Ten bounded regression cases use actual spawned workers, covering both train/eval with failures in initialization, action selection, transition recording and parent environment stepping, plus healthy controls. A watchdog makes the old hang observable without leaving test processes behind.

- Unchanged-source [minimum Linux](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43835177617/job/133189898650), [latest Linux](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43835177617/job/133189898888) and [latest Windows](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43835177617/job/133189898564) trainer jobs each report **8 failed, 22 passed, 34 skipped**: six worker-failure hangs and two parent-failure process leaks.
- The fixed [Torch workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43836910799) passes all **9 jobs**. All three trainer suites report **30 passed, 34 skipped**.
- All configured [pre-commit hooks](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43836910899) pass.

This handles Python exceptions in worker tasks and parent execution. It does not add detection for workers killed externally without raising a Python exception.

prs.title: Support callable learning-rate scheduler factories
prs.head: 0ca4acce49b6f92998c9030a98b918cf0146876c
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #541

## Problem

Scheduler initialization reads `__qualname__` directly from the configured factory. Partials and callable factory objects therefore raise `AttributeError`. Wrappers returning `KLAdaptiveLR` also lose adaptive stepping because classification examines the wrapper instead of the returned schedule.

## Change

Construct the schedule first, then use an explicit `kl_adaptive = True` marker and `is_kl_adaptive` helper to identify adaptive schedules. Apply the same initialization sequence in JAX A2C, PPO, RPO, IPPO and MAPPO, and Warp PPO. The marker, helper, documentation and helper unit tests incorporate [Toni-SM's follow-up patch](https://github.com/Toni-SM/skrl/pull/542#issuecomment-6927131467). Ordinary unmarked schedules keep the ordinary path, regardless of their names.

Public-Runner regressions cover eight factory/schedule forms across all six affected algorithms. Each test performs two rollout updates, checks finite changed policy parameters, and verifies the expected KL-adaptive learning rate where applicable. The added marker controls cover a marked custom callable without `__qualname__` and an unmarked ordinary schedule with a misleading adaptive name. Scheduler helper tests are included in the existing minimum/latest JAX and Warp CI jobs.

## Validation

Current head `0ca4acce49b6f92998c9030a98b918cf0146876c`:

- The two scheduler-helper files and two Runner regression files: **52 passed**.
- The same Runner regressions against the preceding implementation: **12 failed, 36 passed**, reproducing both marker-classification cases across all six algorithms.
- `pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Local CPU validation used Python 3.12.14, JAX/jaxlib 0.4.31, flax 0.9.0, optax 0.2.5, Warp 1.15.0 and warp-nn 0.4.1. The upstream workflows for this head await maintainer approval.

- Fork CI on this exact head: [JAX](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/44005662856) and [Warp](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/44005881758) each passed all three latest-dependency jobs (components, environments and utilities), for **6 successful jobs**. The minimum-dependency jobs are skipped by the existing manual-dispatch conditions; the current-head remote minimum matrix is not claimed as rerun.

Earlier factory-compatibility validation:

- [JAX baseline](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43834104083): trainer suite 25 failed, 21 passed, 22 skipped.
- [Warp baseline](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43834104038): trainer suite 5 failed, 11 passed, 12 skipped.
- At `dde082b6`, [JAX](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43837059370) and [Warp](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43837059342) each passed all six workflow jobs on minimum/latest dependencies, and [pre-commit](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43837059392) passed. These workflow results predate the marker follow-up.

This fixes factory compatibility and adaptive-schedule identification independently of #512's absolute learning-rate handling.

prs.title: Keep singleton advantage normalization finite during PPO updates
prs.head: 0e2462713dab6bc4afd8402411c5b73c71cad14b
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

A valid one-transition, unmasked rollout produces NaN advantages because `torch.std` uses the sample correction with one element. Both discrete and continuous dataset preparation paths use this expression. The NaN then poisons model parameters during an actual PPO update.

## Change

Use population variance for the singleton case while preserving the existing sample standard deviation for larger batches. Route the two dataset preparation paths and the unmasked normalization helper through the shared implementation.

The regressions cover both public normalization helpers, both dataset preparation paths, central-value forwarding, masked controls, float32/float64, constant and varying batches, and a real one-transition continuous PPO rollout and optimizer update.

## Validation

- [Test-only baseline](https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43844181128): 11 regression failures; Python 3.11 and 3.14 logs each show 439 passed, 16 skipped alongside those failures.
- [Fixed workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43844717527): all six jobs passed, including Python 3.11–3.14, lint and lock validation. Python 3.11 and 3.14 each report **450 passed, 16 skipped**.

Validated head: `0e2462713dab6bc4afd8402411c5b73c71cad14b`.

This covers the unmasked singleton case. #379 addresses cancellation in masked variance and #365 addresses moving-statistics normalization; neither handles this path.

prs.title: Stabilize gradients through smoothed PPO clipping
prs.head: 05a5c0426d1b863f16b625b14b58524dbb0fca1b
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

The explicit exponential in `smooth_clamp` can overflow even for ordinary finite PPO log-ratios. With `e_clip=0.01` and a log-ratio of -1, the forward result is finite but backward produces NaN gradients. This occurs for both advantage signs and poisons parameters in a real PPO update using `use_smooth_clamp=True`.

## Change

Evaluate the same sigmoid expression through `torch.sigmoid`, avoiding the overflowing intermediate. The clipping curve and existing loss selection are unchanged.

Add forward/gradient checks against a float64 reference, finite-gradient cases across float16, bfloat16, float32 and float64 and three clip widths, non-PPO controls, and an actual PPO optimizer update with finite log-ratios.

## Validation

- [Test-only baseline](https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43844187325): 13 regression failures; Python 3.11 and 3.14 logs each show 441 passed, 16 skipped alongside those failures.
- [Fixed workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43844722137): all six jobs passed, including Python 3.11–3.14, lint and lock validation. Python 3.11 and 3.14 each report **454 passed, 16 skipped**.

Validated head: `05a5c0426d1b863f16b625b14b58524dbb0fca1b`.

The original smooth-clipping implementation was introduced in #126. This change fixes its numerical evaluation without changing standard PPO clipping.

prs.title: Apply pending seeds when Gymnasium vector environments reset
prs.head: 72f09f5ac8efac282730884398b7eb8d137df205
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

`GymnasiumVecEnv.seed(seed)` records a value that reset never consumes. Reseeding therefore fails to reproduce initial observations in both synchronous and asynchronous native vector environments and in custom manual environments. The manual path also ignores the constructor's seed.

## Change

Keep a pending reset seed, pass it to the next reset, and consume it once. Manual environments receive distinct `seed + index` values. Subsequent unseeded resets continue each environment's random stream.

The regression suite uses real CartPole environments with one and three actors, seeds 0 and 42, native sync and async execution, and manual vectorization. A recording environment verifies that explicit seeds are applied exactly once and forwarded with the per-environment offset.

## Validation

- [Unchanged-source baseline](https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43845016794): 14 failed, 413 passed, 16 skipped in the Python 3.11 and 3.14 jobs.
- [Fixed workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43845537271): all six jobs passed, including Python 3.11–3.14, lint and lock validation. Python 3.11 and 3.14 each report **427 passed, 16 skipped**.

Validated head: `72f09f5ac8efac282730884398b7eb8d137df205`.

#332 fixes Runner seed parsing; this addresses the vector environment's public reset-seeding path.

prs.title: Preserve terminal observations across manual autoresets
prs.head: 12bdee7868e17c5afdd14f3a747a40ea57e6c984
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

The manual Gymnasium vector path resets a completed environment before returning its observation, discarding the true terminal state. SAC already consumes `info["final_observation"]` for same-step truncation bootstrapping, but this wrapper never supplies it. Replay therefore falls back to the preceding state even when the wrapper had the exact terminal observation.

## Change

Capture completed environments' observations before reset, including environments that reuse observation buffers. Return the batched `final_observation` and its validity mask with the existing same-step result. Preserve array, nested dictionary and central-state layouts, using placeholders only for rows marked invalid. Live-only steps retain the existing info shape.

The regressions cover mixed live/completed environments, one and multiple agents, termination and truncation, nested observations and central states. An actual SAC rollout verifies that truncated replay entries contain terminal step 3 rather than the previous step 2. A live-only control checks that terminal-observation output is absent until needed.

## Validation

- [Unchanged-source baseline](https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43845027664): Python 3.12 and 3.13 each report 25 failed, 414 passed, 16 skipped, including the actual SAC replay regression.
- [Fixed workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43845542623): all six jobs passed, including Python 3.11–3.14, lint and lock validation. Python 3.11 and 3.14 each report **439 passed, 16 skipped**.

Validated head: `12bdee7868e17c5afdd14f3a747a40ea57e6c984`.

#356 introduced the same-step metadata and SAC consumer; this supplies the missing terminal observations at the manual vector boundary.

prs.title: Honor vector environment action masks during evaluation
prs.head: 28f495d887c0cd1847d2234844b77a223e540e1d
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

`BasePlayer.run()` only checks the legacy singular `has_action_mask()` / `get_action_mask()` methods. Vector environments expose the plural `has_action_masks()` / `get_action_masks()` interface, so a trained discrete policy can choose invalid actions during evaluation even though training uses the masks.

## Changes

- Select the vector environment mask interface when it is supported.
- Retain the legacy singular interface, including subclasses that inherit the default `IVecEnv.has_action_masks() == False` implementation.
- Exercise `PpoPlayerDiscrete.run()` with real discrete and multi-discrete networks, deterministic and sampled actions, and both mask protocols. The test policy strongly prefers an invalid action, making dropped masks observable at the environment boundary.

## Validation

The 16 added cases fail in 4 vector-interface cases before the fix; legacy and unmasked controls pass. The full suite changes from **4 failed, 425 passed, 16 skipped** to **429 passed, 16 skipped** on both Python 3.11 and 3.14. The existing CI's lock, lint, and all four Python 3.11–3.14 test jobs pass.

- Before: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43846644104
- After: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43847142850

This addresses player-side mask discovery, separately from the model-side multi-discrete masking fixed in #361.

prs.title: Handle full and partially written evaluation checkpoints
prs.head: 1245933f37e9e618b486028e26874f51e3505a38
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

The evaluation worker probes a checkpoint with `torch.load()` before calling `restore()`. That probe uses the newer weights-only default even though the normal checkpoint loader supports complete training state, including NumPy environment state. On any load failure, the exception clause references `torch.TorchError`, which does not exist; the resulting `AttributeError` stops evaluation instead of rejecting an incomplete file.

## Changes

- Match the existing `torch_ext.safe_load()` behavior by probing the full checkpoint with `weights_only=False`.
- Catch the concrete exceptions produced by missing, empty, truncated, or invalid checkpoint files.
- Keep the worker's existing behavior of clearing a rejected checkpoint and accepting the next checkpoint.

The regression tests exercise actual Torch serialization and the existing checkpoint loader, including tensor-only and NumPy-containing states, partial files followed by recovery, missing files, restore failures, and an empty queue.

## Validation

The full suite changes from **5 failed, 416 passed, 16 skipped** before the fix to **421 passed, 16 skipped** after it on both Python 3.11 and 3.14. The existing CI's lock, lint, and all four Python 3.11–3.14 test jobs pass.

- Before: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43846653545
- After: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43847151332

prs.title: Retain balanced evaluation statistics across environment resets
prs.head: f2dc1a1d9dcdddafe1c74b641283cf9be9d332bf
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

With `player.balance_env_rewards: true`, `BasePlayer.run()` recreates the per-environment totals inside the outer reset loop. For a single environment, every completed episode starts another outer iteration, so the final summary contains only the last episode. Vector environments also lose earlier totals when `player.max_steps` ends a rollout and the outer loop resets them.

For example, three episodes with returns 2, 8, and 20 are reported as an average of 20 instead of 10.

## Changes

Initialize the per-environment totals once, after the batch size is known, and retain them through subsequent resets within the same evaluation run. Current-episode rewards and lengths still reset normally.

Regression coverage runs real `PpoPlayerDiscrete` networks through single and vector environment evaluation, both four-value and Gymnasium five-value step APIs, optional scores, and ordinary unbalanced reporting as a control. The assertions check the final reward, length, and score summaries against the complete episode sequence.

## Validation

The full suite changes from **8 failed, 421 passed, 16 skipped** before the fix to **429 passed, 16 skipped** after it on Python 3.11 and 3.14. All six existing CI jobs pass, including lock, lint, and Python 3.11–3.14 tests.

- Before: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43848422988
- After: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43848995529

prs.title: Preserve MLP widths with first-layer-only normalization
prs.head: 0ec982ab311b738065ef74a21c6b0056974f9c82
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

With `mlp.norm_only_first_layer: true` and layer or batch normalization, the sequential MLP builder skips `in_size = unit` after the first normalized layer. A network such as `[16, 8, 4]` therefore constructs its third layer with 16 input features even though the second layer returns 8. Both PPO and SAC crash on their first forward pass.

## Changes

Update the next layer's input width as soon as each dense layer is added, independently of whether that layer receives normalization. The normalization placement remains controlled by the existing option.

The regression matrix exercises PPO shared and separate actor/critic networks and SAC actor/twin-critic networks. It covers changing and constant widths, layer and batch normalization, first-layer-only and all-layer normalization, and the unnormalized control. Every working case performs a forward and backward pass and checks finite gradients.

## Validation

Before the fix, six changing-width configurations fail with a matrix dimension mismatch. On Python 3.11 and 3.14 the full suite changes from **6 failed, 443 passed, 16 skipped** to **449 passed, 16 skipped**. All six existing CI jobs pass, including lock, lint, and the Python 3.11–3.14 matrix.

- Before: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43849416450
- After: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43849994662

#343 propagated the normalization options into this builder; this fixes the dimension tracking inside the resulting first-layer-only path.

prs.title: Share coordinate convolution grids across actor batches
prs.head: d6fa06f925abdc4e63e2da9baa1de10a426b4f9d
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

`CoordConv2d` caches a fully repeated coordinate grid for every batch size. The coordinates are identical for all actors, but a float32 grid for 1,024 actors with 84×84 images retains **57,802,752 bytes**. Encountering different rollout, minibatch, and evaluation batch sizes retains additional copies.

## Changes

Cache one spatial grid per image shape, dtype, and device, then expose the requested batch through an expanded view. The same example retains **56,448 bytes**, a **1,024× reduction in coordinate-cache storage**. Including the full device in the key also keeps grids on their requested device. Explicit `align_corners=False` preserves the existing affine-grid default.

The convolution still receives the same coordinate values. Tests compare both outputs and input/parameter gradients against an explicitly repeated-grid reference for rectangular and single-row images in float32 and float64. Additional checks measure backing-storage bytes, reuse across batch sizes, and dtype/device preservation.

## Validation

Before the change, five storage assertions fail while all numerical equivalence checks pass. On Python 3.11 and 3.14 the full suite changes from **5 failed, 426 passed, 16 skipped** to **431 passed, 16 skipped**. All six existing CI jobs pass, including lock, lint, and Python 3.11–3.14 tests.

- Before: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43849546234
- After: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43850434142

The storage measurement is for cached coordinate tensors; no end-to-end training throughput claim is made.

prs.title: Preserve SAC MLP trunks when attaching actor and critic heads
prs.head: 3d0be31b0190f2c71494371d2728a5a126df79c7
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

SAC locates the final direct `Linear` child of each MLP and rebuilds the trunk from its children when attaching output heads. A D2RL trunk exposes `ModuleList` children, so constructing an SAC actor or critic with `mlp.d2rl: true` raises `StopIteration`. Flattening that trunk would also discard the skip connections implemented by its forward method. An empty hidden-layer list fails for the same output-head lookup.

## Changes

Append output heads using the final nested linear layer's output width, falling back to the input width for an empty sequential trunk. Preserve custom trunk modules as modules so their forward method and skip connections remain active. Keep the existing flat parameter keys for ordinary sequential trunks.

The 16 regression cases build actual SAC actor and double-Q networks, run forward/backward passes, and round-trip their state dictionaries. They cover D2RL and sequential trunks, multiple depths, layer/batch/no normalization, empty sequential trunks, and existing checkpoint key compatibility.

## Validation

On Python 3.11 and 3.14, the unchanged implementation produces **9 failed, 420 passed, 16 skipped**; this change produces **429 passed, 16 skipped**. All six existing CI jobs pass, including lock, lint, and Python 3.11–3.14 tests.

- Before: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43850439036
- After: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43851082475

Related: #343 handles the last direct linear layer of sequential SAC trunks; this preserves composite D2RL trunks and handles empty sequential trunks.

prs.title: Prevent timeout bootstrapping for terminated Gymnasium episodes
prs.head: c41d80dbd4794b58d31a7f02e7882922a8f53535
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

A Gymnasium step can report both `terminated=True` and `truncated=True`, for example when the task ends on its time limit. `GymnasiumVecEnv` currently copies `truncated` into `info['time_outs']`. Learners use `done & ~time_outs` to decide whether the transition is terminal, so this combination incorrectly bootstraps a value beyond an actual terminal state.

## Changes

Mark a transition as a timeout only when it is truncated and not terminated. Apply the same precedence to native vector and manual backends, including a timeout flag supplied by a manually wrapped environment. Preserve timeout-only bootstrapping and existing explicit false timeout overrides.

Regression tests cover all termination/truncation combinations, synchronous and asynchronous native vector environments, single/multiple actors, manually wrapped multi-agent environments, and supplied timeout metadata. An actual SAC training/replay test checks the resulting terminal masks used by the learner.

## Validation

On Python 3.11 and 3.14, the full suite changes from **8 failed, 433 passed, 16 skipped** to **441 passed, 16 skipped**. All six existing CI jobs pass, including lock, lint, and Python 3.11–3.14 tests.

- Before: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43851075346
- After: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43851735053

prs.title: Accept the recurrent call contract in IdentityRNN
prs.head: 56714dd65670e5e69dbdb2515075000e2e55ce2e
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

Selecting `rnn.name: identity` fails in an actual A2C network forward pass. The policy calls recurrent modules with `(x, states, dones, bptt_len)`, while `IdentityRNN.forward` still accepts only `(x, states)`, causing a `TypeError` before policy or value outputs are computed.

## Changes

Allow the optional done mask and BPTT length arguments in `IdentityRNN.forward`. The identity module continues returning the exact input and state without modifying either. The existing two-argument call remains supported.

The regression tests compare identity-recurrent policies with corresponding feedforward policies using matching parameters. They check logits, values, input gradients, and unchanged recurrent state across shared/separate actor–critic networks, recurrence before/after the MLP, one/multiple timesteps, and done masks. A separate control retains the original two-argument API.

## Validation

On Python 3.11 and 3.14, the full suite changes from **16 failed, 414 passed, 16 skipped** to **430 passed, 16 skipped**. All six existing CI jobs pass, including lock, lint, and Python 3.11–3.14 tests.

- Before: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43850720342
- After: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43851373284

prs.title: Build multi-discrete policy heads for Impala networks
prs.head: 6e03f6df8a6064c4fa64d20e96ef4322aa5c3c8c
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

`A2CResnetBuilder` reads the `multi_discrete` action-space setting but neither constructs the corresponding policy heads nor returns logits for it. Building the advertised Impala/ResNet configuration therefore ends in a `None` network result instead of a policy distribution. With recurrent previous-action inputs enabled, initialization also tries to add a list of head sizes to an integer input width.

## Changes

Construct and initialize one logits head per discrete action component, and return the list through the existing multi-discrete model interface. For recurrent previous-action inputs, reserve the sum of the head widths and concatenate one-hot encodings of each component.

The 14 regression cases build the real `multi_discrete_a2c` model with an Impala network and exercise sampling, training losses, backward passes, and checkpoint round-trips. The matrix covers feedforward, GRU and LSTM policies, CHW/HWC observations, heterogeneous masked/unmasked heads, and recurrent reward/previous-action inputs.

## Validation

On Python 3.11 and 3.14, the full suite changes from **14 failed, 413 passed, 16 skipped** to **427 passed, 16 skipped**. All six existing CI jobs pass, including lock, lint, and Python 3.11–3.14 tests.

- Before: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43850852161
- After: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43852375377

prs.title: Honor independent optional inputs in recurrent Impala policies
prs.head: 0d4c527ca2689bd6e19064c022e1a8c88097dee1
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

Impala policies expose separate `require_rewards` and `require_last_actions` switches. If either is enabled, the recurrent forward path currently reads both `obs_dict['reward']` and `obs_dict['last_action']` before checking which input is required. A policy configured for only one input therefore raises `KeyError` for the other, unused field.

## Changes

Read and transform each auxiliary input only when its corresponding switch is enabled. Existing behavior when both or neither are enabled is retained.

The 32 regression cases use actual discrete Impala models with GRU/LSTM, recurrence before/after the MLP, CHW/HWC observations, and all four combinations of the two flags. They pass only the requested fields, compare outputs with equivalent calls containing the unused fields, and check finite backward gradients.

## Validation

On Python 3.11 and 3.14, the full suite changes from **16 failed, 429 passed, 16 skipped** to **445 passed, 16 skipped**. All six existing CI jobs pass, including lock, lint, and Python 3.11–3.14 tests.

prs.title: Preserve discrete player action batch and component dimensions
prs.head: ea9e75ce76e0cc7c65b5202f9b7f4c60b41d3003
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

Both discrete player action methods call unrestricted `squeeze()` on their outputs. With a single vector actor this removes the required batch axis: a `Discrete` action becomes scalar and native Gymnasium vector evaluation raises `TypeError`. A one-component multi-discrete action also loses its component axis during sampling, even with multiple actors.

## Changes

Keep action batch and component dimensions throughout deterministic selection and sampling. Remove only the leading synthetic batch axis for an unbatched environment. Apply the same shape contract to masked and unmasked actions.

The 38 regression cases run real `PpoPlayerDiscrete` evaluation with unbatched, single-actor and multi-actor observations; Discrete and one/multiple-component Tuple spaces; deterministic/stochastic actions; and masks. Native single-actor CartPole evaluation is included for both action-selection modes.

## Validation

On Python 3.11 and 3.14, the full suite changes from **18 failed, 433 passed, 16 skipped** to **451 passed, 16 skipped**. All six existing CI jobs pass, including lock, lint, and Python 3.11–3.14 tests.

prs.title: Disable autograd during SAC player inference
prs.head: d7b8dee76c9dab1aeaee58b5fa5b61b3eb5d27ce
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

`SACPlayer.get_action` evaluates its actor with autograd enabled. The unbatched path detaches the result, but the vector path does not. Consequently, deterministic SAC evaluation with a NumPy vector environment fails when `BasePlayer.env_step` converts actions to NumPy. Both deterministic and sampled inference also save unnecessary tensors for a backward pass that evaluation never performs.

## Changes

Evaluate SAC actions under `torch.no_grad()`, covering observation normalization, actor evaluation, sampling/mean selection and per-dimension action rescaling. Returned values and action bounds are unchanged, and the caller's gradient-mode context is restored normally.

The 28 regression cases cover unbatched/single-actor/multi-actor evaluation, NumPy/tensor environments, deterministic/stochastic actions, input normalization, exact output agreement with a no-grad reference, and absence of saved backward tensors. Native Gymnasium Pendulum evaluation reproduces the original NumPy-conversion error.

## Validation

On Python 3.11 and 3.14, the full suite changes from **11 failed, 430 passed, 16 skipped** to **441 passed, 16 skipped**. All six existing CI jobs pass, including lock, lint, and Python 3.11–3.14 tests.

- Before: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43853346750
- After: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43853964027

Related: #290 corrects the deterministic action-selection condition; this addresses autograd during that evaluation path.

prs.title: Honor sigma parametrization and logstd bounds in Impala policies
prs.head: 2a58b76d855839234fecb4697b78e2d55b3569b8
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

Continuous Impala policies read sigma floors and ceilings, but do not retain `sigma_parametrization` or `logstd_bounds` from their action-space configuration. The shared model consequently falls back to unbounded exponential parametrization, silently ignoring requested softplus/linear/scalar transforms and configured log-standard-deviation bounds. The same settings already work with `A2CBuilder`.

## Changes

Read these settings in `A2CResnetBuilder` and resolve the `scalar` compatibility alias consistently with the ordinary actor–critic builder. The existing shared distribution code then applies the configured transform and bounds. Omitted settings preserve the previous default.

The 60 regression cases exercise real continuous Impala models with global/state-dependent sigma heads, default/exp/softplus/linear/scalar settings, negative/interior/large raw outputs, and optional sigma ceilings. They compare standard deviations, log probabilities, entropy, and sigma gradients to independent distribution calculations, and run a full policy/value backward pass.

## Validation

On Python 3.11 and 3.14, the full suite changes from **44 failed, 429 passed, 16 skipped** to **473 passed, 16 skipped**. All six existing CI jobs pass, including lock, lint, and Python 3.11–3.14 tests.

- Before: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43854154544
- After: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43854841226

prs.title: Construct LayerNorm for recurrent Impala policies when requested
prs.head: f372f7773c927810e3d9ebc50e41e4b18c585fb0
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

Setting `rnn.layer_norm: true` on an Impala policy raises `AttributeError` during its first forward pass. The forward path calls `self.layer_norm`, but the constructor still contains only a commented-out creation of that module.

## Changes

Create the recurrent LayerNorm when the option is enabled, using the recurrent output width. No additional parameters are introduced when it is disabled.

The 16 regression cases build actual discrete Impala policies with GRU/LSTM, recurrence before/after the MLP, CHW/HWC observations, and normalization on/off. They exercise forward/backward passes, finite nonzero LayerNorm gradients, the correct recurrent width when the MLP width differs, and state-dictionary round-trips.

## Validation
