prs.title: Exclude next-step reset rows from player statistics and RNN state
prs.head: bf0b09e21a4236975b6b892175457e79daf74560
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

With `autoreset_mode: next_step`, a vector environment consumes an extra step after termination to reset that actor. Its action is ignored and its observation belongs to the previous episode. `BasePlayer.run` counts that reset-only row as a real episode step. A recurrent player also advances its freshly cleared hidden state using the terminal observation and carries that state into the new episode.

For staggered two- and three-step episodes, the existing evaluation loop reports an average length of 3.0 instead of 2.5. Native two-actor Gymnasium evaluation with a two-step time limit also counts the intervening resets.

## Changes

Track the previous done flags for next-step environments, accumulate statistics only for live rows, and clear recurrent state after the ignored reset step as well as after termination. The existing environment metadata selects this behavior; same-step environments retain their current accounting.

The 27 regression cases exercise real feedforward, GRU and LSTM players, NumPy/tensor environments, balanced/unbalanced summaries, staggered episode endings, and native Gymnasium CartPole. Recurrent checks verify zero state at each new episode's initial observation.

## Validation

On Python 3.11 and 3.14, the full suite changes from **15 failed, 425 passed, 16 skipped** to **440 passed, 16 skipped**. All six existing CI jobs pass, including lock, lint, and Python 3.11–3.14 tests.

- Before: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43854730470
- After: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43855454969

Related: #356 and #362 handle reset-only rows during SAC/PPO training. This applies the declared autoreset contract to player evaluation.

prs.title: Track masked running normalization per feature and valid row
prs.head: ca4535ca1f90ee0c87ed6b82f3f41ab83c5bfc22
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

The masked `RunningMeanStd` update delegates to a pooled scalar-moment helper, although the unmasked normalizer tracks separate feature/channel statistics. It also adds the full input batch length to its count, including masked-out rows. Depending on shape, row masks either broadcast incorrectly or produce pooled statistics; excluded NaN padding can also poison persistent state through multiplication by zero.

## Changes

Select valid rows before computing moments, use the normalizer's existing reduction axes and population-variance convention, and increment the running count by the number of selected rows. An empty masked selection leaves the prior unchanged. Both one-dimensional and column row masks are supported.

The 40 regression cases compare each update against feeding the actual valid rows to an unmasked normalizer. They cover feature and per-channel layouts, Boolean/float masks, eager/TorchScript execution, repeated updates, zero/one valid rows, NaN padding, normalization/denormalization, and state-dictionary restoration.

## Validation

On Python 3.11 and 3.14, the full suite changes from **40 failed, 413 passed, 16 skipped** to **453 passed, 16 skipped**. All six existing CI jobs pass, including lock, lint, and Python 3.11–3.14 tests.

- Before: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43854739055
- After: https://github.com/Afloat16/rl_games/actions/runs/43855464462

Related: #379 addresses pooled masked moments and #399 handles physically empty input batches. This change corrects featurewise statistics and sample counts for nonempty masked normalization calls.

prs.title: Preserve static tensor conditions across XM chunks
prs.head: cfc23bd025f064fade4f1122b4d6de43a90a2ceb
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

XM identifies batch tensors before repeating candidates, but identifies them again by their leading size when slicing each chunk. A static condition tensor whose leading size happens to equal `batch * candidates` is therefore sliced even though it was never repeated.

For a batch of two sequences, three candidates, and a six-element feature-scale vector, chunk sizes two and four raise a dimension mismatch. A chunk size of one broadcasts each sliced scalar instead, silently changing the loss from 0.6805501580 to 0.5338293314 in the regression.

## Change

Retain each input leaf's original batch classification and use it for both candidate expansion and chunk slicing. Static tensors stay intact, while nested batched conditions and shared timesteps continue to follow the candidates.

## Validation

- Native `GaussianDiffusion1D` with a conditional PyTorch model and nested `model_forward_kwargs`.
- Unchanged implementation: **3 failed, 1 passed**. Fixed implementation: **4 passed**.
- Chunk sizes 1, 2, 4 and the complete expanded batch verify the loss, model-parameter gradients, condition-vector gradients, and caller dictionary ownership.
- New-test Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass.

Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu. The unchanged upstream tree has no tracked test suite or PR workflow.

[Before test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/d700aa6c96126ea79e348e459e3f6bb60f18a7dd/contribution-audit/xm-static-before.log) · [After test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/d700aa6c96126ea79e348e459e3f6bb60f18a7dd/contribution-audit/xm-static-after.log)

prs.title: Keep immiscible noise assignment outside autograd
prs.head: 1196b99a3b4aa136ab004ebca48adfd4c72653ea
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

Immiscible training sends the pairwise distance tensor directly to SciPy's linear assignment solver. If an image or a supplied noise tensor requires gradients, the distances also require gradients and SciPy's NumPy conversion raises before the model can train.

The discrete assignment does not have a gradient, but the selected noise and the forward diffusion still need to retain their gradient paths.

## Change

Run only `noise_assignment` under `torch.no_grad()`. The returned permutation is then applied outside that context, preserving gradients to the images, selected noise and model parameters.

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **3 failed, 1 passed**. Fixed implementation: **4 passed**.
- Native `GaussianDiffusion.p_losses` with image gradients, noise gradients, both, and neither.
- A known two-sample optimal assignment is compared with an independent forward-diffusion/loss calculation; all requested input and parameter gradients are finite, nonzero and match the reference.
- The regression uses `pred_x0` and no offset noise, so it reproduces independently of the assigned-noise target fix in #375 and offset ownership fix in #399.
- New-test Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

[Before test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/d0cbbfad26862ec8b17e4ffdcfc7728d3d3703b2/contribution-audit/immiscible-before.log) · [After test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/d0cbbfad26862ec8b17e4ffdcfc7728d3d3703b2/contribution-audit/immiscible-after.log)

prs.title: Accept int32 labels in all Karras U-Net variants
prs.head: f8fe6046eef2ee82cc299162beca18ebea44a099
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

All three Karras U-Net variants recognize both `torch.int` (int32) and `torch.long` class labels, but pass them unchanged to `F.one_hot`, which requires long tensors. Valid int32 label batches therefore fail before the class projection.

## Change

Convert the integer indices to long before one-hot encoding in the 1D, 2D and 3D models. This groups the three occurrences of the same failure into one correction.

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **3 failed, 3 passed**. Fixed implementation: **6 passed**.
- Native small 1D, 2D and 3D Karras U-Nets, with int32 regressions and int64 controls.
- Outputs and every trainable parameter gradient match an independent copy receiving int64 labels exactly. Class-projection gradients are nonzero.
- This failure reproduces with ordinary float32 models, before the projection-dtype issue addressed in #396.
- New-test Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

[Before test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/d0cbbfad26862ec8b17e4ffdcfc7728d3d3703b2/contribution-audit/karras-int32-before.log) · [After test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/d0cbbfad26862ec8b17e4ffdcfc7728d3d3703b2/contribution-audit/karras-int32-after.log)

prs.title: Normalize FP16 activations safely in RMSNorm
prs.head: a530d2c36966c45e996352cb7d29a98351d0062b
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

The RMSNorm implementations normalize directly in float16. For an all-zero feature vector, the default normalization epsilon of `1e-12` underflows, producing NaNs. For eight finite features of 40000, the float16 vector norm overflows, producing an incorrect all-zero output.

The same operation appears in the standard, 1D, classifier-free, guided, RePaint and simple-diffusion variants.

## Change

Evaluate normalization in float32 for float16 inputs and cast the normalized values back before applying the existing gain and scale. Float32/float64 paths, normalization axes and the existing scale factors are preserved.

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **12 failed, 24 passed**. Fixed implementation: **36 passed**.
- All six native RMSNorm classes, float16/float32/float64, zero vectors and large finite vectors.
- Analytic expected outputs, preserved output dtype, finite input gradients and expected gain gradients under a squared-loss backward pass.
- New-test Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

The tests cover these stated inputs and backward losses; no full training or GPU benchmark is claimed.

[Before test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/d0cbbfad26862ec8b17e4ffdcfc7728d3d3703b2/contribution-audit/rms-before.log) · [After test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/d0cbbfad26862ec8b17e4ffdcfc7728d3d3703b2/contribution-audit/rms-after.log)

prs.title: Initialize DDPM and DDIM noise in the diffusion dtype
prs.head: 0dbc3e5c9872363300a447a860a63751c6e34810
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

The discrete DDPM and DDIM samplers create their initial noise in the global default dtype. After a diffusion wrapper is converted with `.double()` or `.half()`, that noise is still float32 and the first convolution can fail with a dtype mismatch.

This occurs in the standard, 1D, guided, RePaint and classifier-free variants.

## Change

Initialize the sampling noise in the registered diffusion buffers' dtype in both sampling paths. The default float32 behavior is preserved, and the change does not require the denoiser to expose a particular parameter.

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **20 failed, 10 passed**. Fixed implementation: **30 passed**.
- All five native diffusion wrappers, DDPM and DDIM, and float32/float64/float16.
- Real PyTorch convolutional denoisers verify the first sampled tensor against an independently seeded generator, every denoiser input's dtype, the expected number of denoising steps, and finite outputs of the expected shape and dtype.
- This isolates the sampler's initial allocation; the separate sinusoidal embedding issue in #370 is not changed.
- New-test Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

[Before test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/2637422487b8a5eecda5c292323971fd9a275e69/contribution-audit/sampling-dtype-before.log) · [After test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/2637422487b8a5eecda5c292323971fd9a275e69/contribution-audit/sampling-dtype-after.log)

prs.title: Honor explicit full_attn=False in image U-Nets
prs.head: 66c73d79c968edb1f5f05a20665569148b38316b
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

The standard and RePaint U-Nets use `if not full_attn` to choose their default stage configuration. An explicit `full_attn=False` is therefore replaced by the default tuple, which enables full attention in the final encoder/decoder stage.

The scalar setting should behave like an explicit tuple of `False` values. Currently it silently chooses a different architecture and attention cost.

## Change

Apply the default configuration only when `full_attn is None`. Explicit boolean values continue through the existing stage expansion. The dedicated bottleneck attention is unchanged.

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **4 failed, 8 passed**. Fixed implementation: **12 passed**.
- Both native U-Nets, one and two stages, and `False`, `True` and `None` controls.
- Encoder/decoder attention classes, full forward outputs and all trainable parameter gradients are checked against independently initialized models receiving the equivalent explicit stage tuple.
- New-test Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

[Before test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/2637422487b8a5eecda5c292323971fd9a275e69/contribution-audit/explicit-attn-before.log) · [After test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/2637422487b8a5eecda5c292323971fd9a275e69/contribution-audit/explicit-attn-after.log)

prs.title: Skip unused sampling noise when stochastic updates are disabled
prs.head: 6451548d85b0ff4650883e4c3d00183e64a9a5c3
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

DDIM generates a full per-step Gaussian noise tensor even when `eta=0`, so the update immediately multiplies it by zero. The EDM Heun sampler does the same when churn is disabled or the current noise level is outside the churn interval.

These allocations and random-number generation scale with the sample size and number of steps.

## Change

Draw DDIM step noise only when `eta != 0`, and EDM perturbations only when `gamma != 0`. Apply the DDIM correction to the standard, 1D, guided, RePaint and classifier-free implementations together.

The 1D `return_noise=True` path retains its existing draws and returned tensor; the separate auxiliary-return correction in #386 is not included here.

Skipping unused draws intentionally advances the random state less. A seeded trajectory can therefore change when later active perturbations or stochastic denoiser layers consume that state; the sampling coefficients and active-noise distributions are preserved.

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **8 failed, 8 passed**. Fixed implementation: **16 passed**.
- All five native DDIM samplers with zero/nonzero eta, including convolutional denoisers, an independent first-transition calculation, RNG state and real random-call counts.
- Four-step deterministic DDIM eliminates three unused full-sample draws.
- Native EDM covers disabled churn, an excluded interval, fully active churn and a mixed active/inactive schedule. An independent linear-ODE Heun calculation checks outputs and consumed draws.
- Four-step EDM with no active churn eliminates four unused full-sample draws.
- New-test Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

[Before test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/4a88cfb4721a44be1a1c0d31938ac38694205224/contribution-audit/inactive-noise-before.log) · [After test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/4a88cfb4721a44be1a1c0d31938ac38694205224/contribution-audit/inactive-noise-after.log)

prs.title: Share XM random inputs when optional values are None
prs.head: b6d941c0b94caa0484dc08158e069a241dfe2355
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

The diffusion APIs use `None` to mean “sample a default time or condition-drop mask.” XM instead checks only whether those keyword names exist.

Passing `times=None` or `cond_keep_mask=None` therefore skips XM's shared sampling. Each expanded candidate or chunk then samples independently, so candidates for the same training example can be compared at different noise levels or with different conditioning. In the native classifier-free regression, passing both defaults explicitly changes the loss from 0.85029346 to 0.71974432.

## Change

Treat an absent key and an explicit `None` consistently when injecting the shared random inputs. Concrete caller-provided times and masks still take precedence.

This changes the wrapper's handling of existing optional arguments. It does not incorporate the diffusion-API additions in #398 or the static-tensor chunk correction in #411.

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **14 failed, 10 passed**. Fixed implementation: **24 passed**.
- Native standard, 1D, continuous-time, velocity-parameterized continuous-time and classifier-free diffusion training.
- Chunk sizes two and six compare omitted/default-`None` calls under the same random seed, checking exact losses, all model-parameter gradients and identical time/condition values within each candidate group.
- Explicit tensor inputs remain unchanged and produce the same values and gradients as the reference.
- New-test Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

[Before test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/4a88cfb4721a44be1a1c0d31938ac38694205224/contribution-audit/xm-none-before.log) · [After test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/4a88cfb4721a44be1a1c0d31938ac38694205224/contribution-audit/xm-none-after.log)

prs.title: Accept the diffusion self-conditioning keyword in KarrasUnet1D
prs.head: 238c0280c4271e0746fd4207ba419eeffe0883bf
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

After #373, `GaussianDiffusion1D` consistently supplies self-conditioning through the `x_self_cond` keyword used by `Unet1D`. `KarrasUnet1D` still accepts only `self_cond`.

Enabling self-conditioning on the native Karras 1D model therefore makes training, DDPM sampling and DDIM sampling fail with an unexpected-keyword error.

## Change

Accept `x_self_cond` as a keyword-only alias while preserving the existing positional and keyword forms of `self_cond`. Supplying both aliases is rejected explicitly rather than choosing one silently. The model's conditioning computation stays unchanged.

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **6 failed, 3 passed**. Fixed implementation: **9 passed**.
- Native `KarrasUnet1D` training, DDPM and DDIM sampling are compared against an independent adapter that routes the diffusion keyword to the original model interface.
- Both enabled and disabled self-conditioning are covered. Training losses, every model-parameter gradient and seeded sampling outputs match exactly.
- Direct legacy positional/keyword calls and the new alias produce identical outputs, conditioning-input gradients and parameter gradients.
- The output gain is set nonzero in the tests so gradients exercise the model rather than a zero-initialized output.
- New-test Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

[Before test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/b0e4db76f43be6f8e6654342bdc6a6024455db3c/contribution-audit/karras1d-selfcond-before.log) · [After test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/b0e4db76f43be6f8e6654342bdc6a6024455db3c/contribution-audit/karras1d-selfcond-after.log)

prs.title: Keep the classifier-free null branch unconditional
prs.head: 5e8c5abf9daf3e7c2d93a4ec4157914699fdcf25
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

`forward_with_cond_scale` forwards `cond_keep_mask` to both the conditional and null prediction. In `forward`, an explicit mask overrides `cond_drop_prob=1`, so samples marked as retained remain conditioned in the supposedly unconditional branch.

With an all-keep mask the two predictions coincide and classifier-free guidance collapses. Mixed masks silently apply the wrong guidance to the retained samples.

## Change

Omit the conditional keep mask only from the null-branch keyword arguments. The conditional prediction still receives the caller's exact mask, and the caller's dictionary is unchanged.

This is independent of the unit-scale return contract in #374 and the zero-variance rescaling case in #376.

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **8 failed, 8 passed**. Fixed implementation: **16 passed**.
- A native classifier-free `Unet` is exercised with default `None`, all-keep, all-drop and mixed masks; guidance scales zero and two; and rescaling coefficients zero and 0.5.
- Null predictions are checked against a separate fully dropped forward pass. Guided outputs are checked against the explicit CFG formula, including rescaling.
- All parameter gradients match the independent reference exactly and remain finite.
- The retained samples are confirmed to have distinct conditional and unconditional predictions, and caller-owned masks are preserved.
- New-test Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

[Before test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/b0e4db76f43be6f8e6654342bdc6a6024455db3c/contribution-audit/cfg-mask-before.log) · [After test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/b0e4db76f43be6f8e6654342bdc6a6024455db3c/contribution-audit/cfg-mask-after.log)

prs.title: Honor split_batches through Accelerate dataloader configuration
prs.head: 3823f87215c0507a58bb39711aa009aee748ad5a
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

Recent Accelerate accepts the legacy `Accelerator(split_batches=...)` argument but no longer applies it to its data-loader configuration. All four trainers still pass that argument, so their default `split_batches=True` silently behaves as `False`.

With a requested batch of 16 and two processes, each process receives 16 examples instead of eight. The effective global batch doubles, increasing per-process memory and changing the intended training batch.

## Change

Pass `split_batches` through `DataLoaderConfiguration` in the standard, 1D, guided and RePaint trainers. Preserve the explicit `False` behavior. Declare `accelerate>=0.28.0`, the version that exports this configuration API.

This corrects batch sharding independently of the gradient-accumulation synchronization change in #403.

## Validation

- Local native-sharding regressions: **8 failed, 4 passed** before; **12 passed** after. These cover the omitted default and explicit `True`/`False` in all four trainers, actual shard contents and a complete optimizer step.
- A separate fork CI job runs **two actual CPU/Gloo processes** with native Accelerate/DDP and all four trainers. Unchanged code: **4 failed, 4 passed**, with every failure caused by local batch size 16 instead of eight.
- Fixed CI: **20 passed** across the native-shard and two-rank suites. Both ranks complete training, receive distinct expected samples and retain identical, finite updated parameters.
- Python 3.12.16, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu, Accelerate 1.15.0 in the distributed run. Local Python 3.12.14. New-test Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass.
- The fork validation uses the same source and test files as this PR; its isolated validation workflow is not included here.

prs.title: Restore training mode in guided and RePaint trainers
prs.head: 08a5e6ea2f9dadf96ce35df6dfc296b9690df4b6
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

The guided and RePaint trainers never restore `self.model.train()`. If the supplied diffusion model is in evaluation mode, or a caller evaluates it between two calls to `train()`, optimization silently continues with evaluation behavior.

Dropout remains disabled and BatchNorm stops updating its running statistics. This produces different parameter updates from the same training call with a model in training mode.

## Change

Restore training mode at the beginning of each optimization iteration, matching the existing standard and 1D trainers.

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **4 failed, 6 passed**. Fixed implementation: **10 passed**.
- Native diffusion training with real convolution, BatchNorm, Dropout, Accelerate and optimizer updates.
- Initially training/evaluating models are covered in all four trainer variants, with the standard and 1D trainers acting as existing-behavior controls.
- Guided and RePaint training is also resumed after an external `eval()` call.
- Layer modes, all updated parameters and BatchNorm buffers match an independently initialized training-mode reference exactly under the same seed; values remain finite.
- New-test Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

prs.title: Keep log-SNR training weights finite without exponentiating SNR
prs.head: 5cfd8be2a20d7bf841578c791aeb286ba25c312b
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

Both simple diffusion and continuous-time min-SNR weighting exponentiate log-SNR before dividing SNR values. Finite schedule outputs can therefore overflow or underflow: `inf / inf` and `0 / 0` make a finite native model loss NaN.

There is also a less extreme failure with the built-in continuous-time cosine schedule: half-precision times near zero produce finite log-SNR values whose exponent overflows FP16. The resulting min-SNR weight becomes zero, silently dropping a training sample that should have a nonzero weight.

## Change

Compute the existing weights in log space. Clip log-SNR at log(gamma), subtract the log denominator, then exponentiate the bounded result. The v-prediction denominator uses stable `softplus(log_snr)`. Half and bfloat16 schedule values use float32 for this weighting calculation.

The formulas and clipping direction are unchanged; disabled clipping and gamma zero remain supported.

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **11 failed, 17 passed**. Fixed implementation: **28 passed**.
- Real UViT and Unet forward/backward passes; per-sample losses and all model parameter gradients checked against an independent 80-digit Decimal evaluation of the original formulas.
- Epsilon/v prediction, clipping disabled or gamma 0/5, FP16/FP32 times, ordinary and extreme finite custom schedules, and the built-in cosine schedule.
- All fixed losses and participating model gradients are finite.
- Ruff checks for the new test (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

[Before test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/daedd5b306c540d72e047f2af6d54fa05533b689/contribution-audit/log-snr-before.log) · [After test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/daedd5b306c540d72e047f2af6d54fa05533b689/contribution-audit/log-snr-after.log)

This addresses numerical evaluation after the clamp-direction correction in #363.

prs.title: Convert the EDM sampling schedule to host scalars once
prs.head: b601299705ad64f4afdfa01cf1877919a654d2ee
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

The EDM Heun sampler converts sigma, next sigma and gamma with three separate `Tensor.item()` calls inside every denoising iteration. A 32-step sample performs 96 individual scalar extractions even though the full schedule is already known before sampling starts.

## Change

Stack the three schedule columns and convert them to Python values once before the loop. The loop uses the same scalar values and keeps the stochastic draws, Heun correction and self-conditioning sequence unchanged.

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **18 failed** on the scalar-extraction regression assertion. Fixed implementation: **18 passed**.
- Real Unet/EDM sampling with 2, 4 and 8 steps; zero, full and partial churn; self-conditioning enabled and disabled.
- Instrumented native sampling reduces the individual `Tensor.item()` calls from **3N to 0**.
- Complete generated tensors and final RNG state match the original per-scalar conversion exactly under the same seed. The reference changes only schedule extraction and uses the same native Heun sampler.
- Ruff checks for the new test (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

[Before test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/daedd5b306c540d72e047f2af6d54fa05533b689/contribution-audit/edm-transfer-before.log) · [After test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/daedd5b306c540d72e047f2af6d54fa05533b689/contribution-audit/edm-transfer-after.log)

prs.title: Publish training checkpoints only after serialization completes
prs.head: d49270235e4ddfe00428c56594935cf1948c9487
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

Each trainer writes checkpoints directly to the final path. If serialization fails after opening an existing `model-latest.pt` or `model-best.pt`, the last usable checkpoint has already been truncated. A failed first save also leaves a partial file at the published checkpoint path.

## Change

Serialize to a temporary file in the same results directory, close it, and atomically replace the destination only after serialization succeeds. Clean up temporary files when serialization or replacement raises. Use one shared helper in the standard, 1D, guided and RePaint trainers.

Checkpoint contents and the loading API remain the same. The previous checkpoint stays available until the replacement is complete.

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **8 failed, 4 passed**. Fixed implementation: **12 passed**.
- Real native diffusion trainers run optimizer updates before saving.
- Simulated partial writes raise during serialization: an existing checkpoint remains byte-for-byte intact and loads its model, optimizer, EMA and step; a failed first save leaves no published checkpoint.
- Successful replacement and full native training-state restoration pass in all four trainer variants; no temporary files remain.
- The guided fixture supplies the pre-existing missing version symbol tracked in #372 so the tests isolate file publication. This patch does not duplicate that import fix.
- New-file Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

prs.title: Match guided training image modes to diffusion channels
prs.head: 862176d2b47fb9380e8e8174b491d13438e0c2a3
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

The guided trainer passes `convert_image_to=None` through to the image dataset. A folder containing grayscale, RGB and RGBA images then produces tensors with different channel counts, so the first training batch fails to stack. Even a uniform folder can disagree with the diffusion model's channel count.

## Change

When no conversion is supplied, infer `L`, `RGB` or `RGBA` from the diffusion model's 1, 3 or 4 channels, matching the standard and RePaint trainers. Explicit conversions and other channel counts retain their current behavior.

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **3 failed, 5 passed**. Fixed implementation: **8 passed**.
- Actual mixed-mode PNG files, native guided Unet/GaussianDiffusion/Trainer, real dataloading and one complete optimizer step.
- Default conversion for 1/3/4 channels matches the corresponding explicit-conversion reference exactly, including every updated model tensor.
- Explicit L/RGB/RGBA and YCbCr settings remain effective; two-channel LA input is preserved.
- Per-image tensors match direct Pillow conversion; training outputs remain finite.
- New-test Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

prs.title: Apply configured attention heads to all linear stages
prs.head: 4ef401fddeec963e1b0782e10b4a93887e7d020c
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

`Unet1D` and the classifier-free `Unet` accept `attn_heads` and `attn_dim_head`, but pass them only to the middle attention layer. Every down/up linear-attention stage silently uses 4 heads of width 32.

For `dim=8, dim_mults=(1, 2), attn_heads=1, attn_dim_head=8`, all four stage QKV projections still have width **384** instead of **24**. Their combined attention parameter count is **20,560**, rather than the requested configuration's **1,360**.

## Change

Pass the existing attention settings to the down/up `LinearAttention` constructors in both variants. This follows the standard 2D Unet, which applies these settings to both full and linear attention stages.

The defaults remain 4 heads of width 32. **Previously saved checkpoints with non-default settings still contain the old fixed-width linear stages; their stage shapes must be matched or migrated before loading into the corrected configuration.**

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **4 failed, 4 passed**. Fixed implementation: **8 passed**.
- Native 1D and classifier-free diffusion losses, backward passes and Adam updates with 1×8, 2×16 and 4×32 attention.
- Actual QKV activation widths, finite model gradients and updated projection weights are checked.
- Omitted defaults and explicit 4×32 configurations have identical state tensors and outputs.
- New-test Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

[Before test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/a770a44e4efc01dd9ec47c59b992f8817a509aff/contribution-audit/linear-attention-config-before.log) · [After test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/a770a44e4efc01dd9ec47c59b992f8817a509aff/contribution-audit/linear-attention-config-after.log) · [Measured widths and parameter counts](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/a770a44e4efc01dd9ec47c59b992f8817a509aff/contribution-audit/linear-attention-metrics.json)

prs.title: Evaluate FID features in the Inception model precision
prs.head: 03bddd76a9ac976872468ddf1682d4c1a8db346d
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

FID passes image tensors directly to its float32 Inception model. Half, bfloat16 and float64 image batches can fail at the first convolution because their dtype differs from the extractor.

An outer autocast context also leaks into feature extraction. On CPU BF16 autocast, complete FID evaluation fails when the resulting BF16 feature tensor is converted to NumPy.

## Change

Convert image inputs to the Inception parameter dtype and locally disable autocast for its forward pass. This keeps feature extraction in the extractor's configured precision without changing the caller's image tensor or outer autocast context.

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **17 failed, 2 passed**. Fixed implementation: **19 passed**.
- Native pytorch-fid Inception wrapper and real first Inception convolutional block, with random weights to avoid network downloads.
- Grayscale/RGB inputs in FP16, BF16, FP32 and FP64, inside and outside CPU BF16 autocast.
- Features match an explicit float32 reference exactly and input tensors remain unchanged.
- Complete dataset statistics, generated statistics and Fréchet-distance evaluation inside autocast match an independent explicit-precision reference.
- These are numerical pipeline tests; they do not evaluate pretrained image quality.
- New-test Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

prs.title: Apply DDPM guidance callbacks without extra keyword arguments
prs.head: c91fa42e77b08ecdcbda95026d8efd0c404000de
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

The guided DDPM sampler calls `cond_fn` only when `guidance_kwargs` is also non-None. Passing a classifier-guidance closure as `sample(cond_fn=...)` therefore silently produces unconditional sampling, even though the callback needs no extra keyword arguments.

## Change

Apply guidance whenever a callback is supplied, treating omitted or None keyword arguments as an empty mapping. Existing explicit mappings are passed through unchanged. This change is limited to DDPM callback dispatch and the mean-conditioning helper.

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **4 failed, 6 passed**. Fixed implementation: **10 passed**.
- Native guided Unet and complete 2-/4-step DDPM trajectories with real autograd gradients of classifier log probabilities.
- Omitted/None/empty/nonempty mappings are covered. Callbacks run at every requested timestep; trajectories match explicit-mapping references exactly under the same seed.
- Sampling without a callback remains unchanged and all generated values are finite.
- New-test Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

prs.title: Keep EDM preconditioning finite across noise scales
prs.head: de956508ed56b49329fdd8b55d1874feaa58297a
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

EDM preconditioning forms `sigma ** 2` and the loss weight multiplies large and small intermediate values. The final mathematical coefficients can be representable while those intermediates overflow.

Examples include finite FP32 sigmas around 1e20 and FP16 sigmas of 500 or 1000. FP16 sigmas near the default lower noise scale also produce an infinite half-precision loss weight, even when the model loss is computed in float32. Native training then yields NaN or infinite losses.

## Change

Use a stable hypotenuse norm for the input, skip and output preconditioning coefficients. Evaluate the algebraically equivalent loss weight as the sum of squared reciprocals. Promote half/bfloat16 coefficient calculations to float32 and retain support for Python scalar sigma values.

## Validation

- Unchanged implementation: **6 failed, 10 passed**. Fixed implementation: **16 passed**.
- Coefficients checked against independent 80-digit Decimal formulas, including ordinary scales, large finite tensor sigmas and a Python scalar of 1e200.
- Native Unet/EDM training across FP16 and FP32 sigma inputs: per-sample losses and every participating model gradient match the high-precision coefficient reference within numerical tolerances and remain finite.
- Native Heun and DPM++ sampling at ordinary and large sigma maxima also match Decimal-coefficient references.
- New-test Ruff checks (`E9,F,I`) and `git diff --check` pass. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu.

[Before test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/a770a44e4efc01dd9ec47c59b992f8817a509aff/contribution-audit/edm-preconditioning-before.log) · [After test output](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/blob/a770a44e4efc01dd9ec47c59b992f8817a509aff/contribution-audit/edm-preconditioning-after.log)

prs.title: Detach running normalization statistics from input autograd graphs
prs.head: 4cbf45225d12b4c6842bc08e06fef21c14fed328
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem and change

`EmpiricalNormalization.update()` updates its running buffers with gradient tracking enabled. When observations come from a differentiable computation, the mean, variance and standard-deviation buffers retain that computation graph. After normalizing and backpropagating one batch, the next independent batch can fail with "Trying to backward through the graph a second time."

Update running statistics under `torch.no_grad()`. The normalization forward pass remains differentiable with respect to its input; the historical statistics remain ordinary buffers.

## Validation

The regression updates and normalizes two independently created differentiable batches, backpropagates each output, checks the expected input gradient `1 / (std + eps)`, and verifies that no running buffer requires gradients.

- On unchanged main, the [baseline run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43815291452/job/133125848787) fails on the second backward pass.
- The [fixed validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43815534089) passes the full suite on Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12; Python 3.12 reports **290 passed, 6 skipped**. The validation branch also includes an independent initial recurrent-state fix. This PR includes only the normalizer change and its regression.
- Lint/pre-commit, documentation, syntax and diff checks pass. CUDA-only tests are skipped.

This concerns the public normalizer API when inputs require gradients. The standard runner collects observations under inference mode and does not reproduce this failure.

Checked upstream PR history and all 47 prior fork branches, including their relevant source variants. This is separate from the existing moment-precision, small-variance and empty-batch normalization changes.

prs.title: Allow implicit zero hidden states in initial recurrent updates
prs.head: f3c16c2cf63f8dd083b55af2b9cf8f01ba64f0aa
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem and change

During the first recurrent rollout, the saved pre-action hidden state is `None`, meaning an all-zero initial state. If the rollout contains one step, storage never receives a later nonempty hidden state from which to allocate its state buffers. The first PPO update therefore fails in `RNN.forward()` with "Hidden states not passed to RNN module during policy update."

Allow the underlying PyTorch GRU/LSTM to use its supported zero initial state when the batch hidden state is `None`.

## Validation

Two regression cases collect a real initial one-step PPO rollout with the standard Gaussian policy, then perform an optimizer update for GRU and LSTM. Both assert finite losses and a parameter change.

- Both cases fail on unchanged main in the [baseline run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43815291452/job/133125848787).
- The [fixed validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43815534089) passes the full suite on Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12; Python 3.12 reports **290 passed, 6 skipped**. This run combines the exact change here with an independent normalizer-autograd fix. This PR includes only the initial-state fix and its two regression cases.
- Lint/pre-commit, documentation, syntax and diff checks pass. CUDA-only tests are skipped.

The prior `fix/recurrent-single-step-time-axis-20261115` fork branch changes `RNNModel.get_latent()` and retains the missing-state exception. This PR does not contain or depend on that time-axis change: its source modification is limited to removing the exception in `RNN.forward()`. Upstream PR history and all 47 prior fork branches were checked for this distinct initial-state failure.

prs.title: Synchronize SAC target normalizers before bootstrapping
prs.head: 37f3700b7f39ae5c85ee510c0a2edf766266f831
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem and change

SAC refreshes the online critics' observation normalizers at the start of `update()`, but the target normalizers are copied only after the first gradient step. The first Bellman target of every iteration therefore uses the previous observation statistics. At the first training update, those target statistics can still be the initial mean and variance from before warm-up.

Copy each updated observation-normalizer buffer to its target before sampling and computing the first target. Target network parameters still follow the existing Polyak update, and target BatchNorm statistics keep their separate behavior.

## Validation

A focused regression collects shifted observations, records the actual input normalization used by the first target critic forward, and compares it with the current online normalizer.

- [Unchanged-source regression](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43858728731/job/133269643109): **1 failed, 275 passed, 6 skipped**. All 64 recorded features differ; the greatest absolute difference is about 99.97.
- [Fixed full suite](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43859106101): Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12 pass. Python 3.12 reports **276 passed, 6 skipped**.
- [Pre-commit](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43859106089) and [documentation](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43859106045) pass.

Validated on upstream `ea39cc2ae4a615c3d70d4ed9055d8b6e3b4c8acd` using CPU CI. The regression does not measure simulator learning performance.

prs.title: Bootstrap PPO timeouts from available final observations
prs.head: 35f8e0a4e30c898083bb2663cf229b1999bdf325
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem and change

When an episode times out, PPO augments its reward using the value predicted before the action. As discussed in #151, this is an approximation when the post-action observation is unavailable. The current VecEnv interface can now provide that observation through `extras["final_obs"]`, but PPO still ignores it.

Use the final observation for the timeout value when it is supplied. Only timeout rows consume those entries, so unused terminal rows can remain undefined. Preserve the recurrent critic's state around this extra forward pass, then perform the normal episode resets. Environments without `final_obs` retain the existing approximation.

The extra critic forward runs only on steps with both final observations and a timeout; it uses the full environment batch to preserve the recurrent batch layout.

## Validation

The regression compares the stored training reward with a separate critic evaluated on the true final observation. It covers MLP, GRU and LSTM critics, includes a genuine terminal episode alongside the timeout, puts NaNs in unused final-observation rows, and checks that continuing recurrent states do not advance.

- [Unchanged source](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43859403424/job/133271939983): **3 failed, 275 passed, 6 skipped**. All three failures are the timeout reward comparison.
- [Fixed full suite](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43860142855): all Python 3.9–3.12 jobs pass; Python 3.12 reports **278 passed, 6 skipped**. Existing legacy timeout and RND logging tests also pass.
- [Pre-commit](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43860142875) and [documentation](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43860142854) pass.

Validated on upstream `ea39cc2ae4a615c3d70d4ed9055d8b6e3b4c8acd` using CPU CI.

prs.title: Avoid duplicate gradient communication for shared PPO encoders
prs.head: b34b56f597bc8ed6b826564ad123a21d0729d3fb
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem and change

With shared CNN encoders, the actor and critic expose the same encoder parameters. `PPO.reduce_parameters()` concatenates both parameter iterators, so every shared gradient is packed and communicated twice per mini-batch. The second average adds no information, but still transfers the shared encoder's gradient payload again.

Deduplicate the parameter iterator before bucketed reduction, preserving its first-occurrence order. Disjoint actor/critic parameters and optional RND parameters retain their existing order and averaging behavior.

## Validation

A new regression runs two real Gloo processes, assigns rank-dependent gradients, and checks both the averaged values and the total bytes passed to the collective. The small bucket size exercises packed gradients and oversized slices.

- Unchanged implementation: 1 failed, 275 passed, 6 skipped. The new test fails because the communicated payload exceeds the unique gradient payload.
- Fixed implementation: 276 passed, 6 skipped. Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12 jobs all pass.
- All configured pre-commit checks and documentation build pass.

[Before test run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43862090443) · [After test run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43862549790)

The change removes redundant communication; these checks do not make a GPU throughput claim.

## Related work

#246 removed duplicate optimizer steps and explicitly left gradient reduction unchanged. This patch addresses the remaining communication cost. It was checked against all upstream PR states and the complete changes of the 58 pre-existing fork branches, including the separate shared-gradient clipping patch.

prs.title: Preserve RMS normalization precision in half ONNX exports
prs.head: e7771da172cc7dff0a4277af031a49546cb8503d
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem and change

The ONNX path in `ResidualMLP.forward()` expands RMS normalization into a square, mean and reciprocal square root. For float16 models, squaring large finite activations overflows in float16. The exported network then returns zeros even though the same native PyTorch network produces finite, nonzero outputs.

Accumulate this export-only normalization in float32 for float16 and bfloat16 activations, and cast back to the original activation dtype after applying the normalization weight. Float32 and float64 retain their existing accumulation precision.

## Validation

The regression exports an actual float16 residual network, executes it with ONNX's `ReferenceEvaluator`, and compares its output with the native model. With inputs `[2000, 4000]`, the unchanged export has 100% relative error and a maximum absolute difference of 1.2646484375; the corrected export matches the native output.

- Before the fix: 1 failed, 275 passed, 6 skipped.
- After the fix: 276 passed, 6 skipped; Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12 all pass.
- All configured pre-commit checks and the documentation build pass.
