prs.title: Preserve double-precision rollout targets and policy likelihoods
prs.head: 849843c5688c11bf14af2fcaeb0a530e810d6507
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem and change

Rollout observations retain their input dtype, but actions, rewards, values, log probabilities and distribution parameters are copied into default float32 buffers. A double-precision actor can therefore assign different likelihoods to its own stored rollout even before any parameter update: action rounding changes the sampled points, and parameter rounding also introduces a spurious KL.

The regression uses a double Gaussian policy with a mean near 1 and a standard deviation of 1e-6. All 32 replayed log probabilities differ on the unchanged implementation, with a maximum absolute error of 0.1565009157863244.

Promote the floating transition buffers when the rollout's first transition requires more precision, and allocate distribution-parameter buffers with sufficient precision. Return and advantage buffers follow the reward/value dtype. Existing float32 buffers are retained for lower-precision inputs, so mixed-precision collection does not narrow them. Promoted buffers are allocated outside inference mode so they remain usable during optimization.

## Validation

The regression collects under inference mode, verifies the unchanged policy's replayed log probabilities and zero KL, checks double reward/return storage, and runs a real PPO update.

- Before the fix: 1 failed, 275 passed, 6 skipped.
- After the fix: 276 passed, 6 skipped; Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12 all pass.
- All configured pre-commit checks and the documentation build pass.

[Before test run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43863417672) · [After test run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43863831949)

## Related work

#264 concerns recurrent hidden-state buffers. This patch addresses the floating transition data used by ordinary feedforward PPO and the shared distillation storage path. Checked all upstream PR states and all 58 pre-existing fork branch deltas; it does not repeat the previous observation or hidden-state dtype changes.

prs.title: Reject invalid bounded-policy action ranges before training
prs.head: f87985faea86669671f8be4da209f491e326476d
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem and change

`SquashedGaussianDistribution` and `BetaDistribution` accept action intervals with equal or reversed endpoints, or nonfinite endpoints. These cannot define the intended affine probability transform: zero width introduces division by zero, negative width makes the log-Jacobian invalid, and nonfinite bounds propagate into actions or densities.

Validate the fixed action bounds once during construction. Require finite endpoints and `min < max` for every action dimension. The squashed Gaussian check retains its scalar/per-dimension broadcasting support.

## Validation

The regressions cover degenerate, reversed and nonfinite bounds in both distribution types, including a per-dimension interval with one invalid actuator.

- Before the fix: 7 failed, 275 passed, 6 skipped; every invalid interval was accepted.
- After the fix: 282 passed, 6 skipped. Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12 all pass, including existing valid-range density and training tests.
- All configured pre-commit checks and the documentation build pass.

[Before test run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43864300731) · [After test run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43864900897)

The checks run only at construction and add no sampling or gradient-step validation.

## Scope

Checked all historical upstream PRs and all 58 pre-existing fork branch deltas. This validates the configured action support; the existing validation-scope patches concern PyTorch's global distribution-validation setting.

prs.title: Respect the epsilon floor when normalizing discounted rewards
prs.head: 63283ad6d2653258970550618be6958608684919
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem and change

`EmpiricalDiscountedVariationNormalization` accepts an `eps` value but divides by every positive empirical standard deviation without using it. Nearly constant returns can therefore amplify rewards far beyond the configured stability scale. With observations `[0.999, 1.001]`, the current path multiplies rewards by approximately 993 even when `eps=0.01` or `eps=0.1`.

Clamp the positive standard-deviation denominator to the configured epsilon. The existing zero-standard-deviation fallback and the unit scaling of a fresh evaluation normalizer remain intact.

## Validation

Two regression cases verify both normalized rewards and input gradients with epsilon values 0.01 and 0.1. Their expected gains are bounded by 100 and 10 respectively.

- Before the fix: 2 failed, 275 passed, 6 skipped.
- After the fix: 277 passed, 6 skipped. Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12 all pass.
- Existing constant-reward, fresh-evaluation, zero-variance and history-ownership regressions continue to pass.
- All configured pre-commit checks and the documentation build pass.

[Before test run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43864811709) · [After test run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43865221515)

## Related work

#258 addresses vector-valued standard deviations. This change addresses the ignored denominator-stability parameter in the existing scalar path. Checked all upstream PR states and the full deltas of the 58 pre-existing fork branches; the regression does not require the old variance-cancellation or moment-precision patches.

prs.title: Keep residual parameter normalization finite in half precision
prs.head: ced6972321fff833ff631aa65629988f91031999
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

`ResidualMLP.normalize_parameters()` computes parameter norms in the parameter dtype. With finite FP16 weights of 20000 and batch-normalization biases of 10000, the squared norm overflows, so normalization replaces a nonzero direction with zeros. Zero rows in linear weights also encounter an epsilon that underflows in half precision. This affects the parameter projection performed after optimizer steps for residual SAC models.

## Change

Compute linear, batch-normalization and RMS parameter normalization in at least float32, then copy the normalized values back into the original parameters. Float32/float64 precision and the parameter dtype are retained.

## Validation

- Regression uses a real `ResidualMLP` with linear, batch-normalization and RMS weights; checks FP16/FP32/FP64 parameters against a float64 reference and verifies finite forward inference.
- Unchanged implementation: **1 failed, 18 passed** in the focused model tests. Fixed independent branch: **273 passed, 6 skipped** in the local suite excluding the Gloo module.
- Combined fork integration with the metric-snapshot and collection fixes: **284 passed, 6 skipped** on Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12, including existing real two-process Gloo tests. Lint and Docs also pass. [Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43894272107).
- All repository pre-commit hooks pass.

This changes post-update parameter projection. The separate ONNX forward RMS normalization fix in #286 addresses another execution path.

prs.title: Snapshot episode metrics before environment buffers are reused
prs.head: 14d1797ff5d70c58e3e43874df2459f64b99ef63
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

`Logger.process_env_step()` queues the environment's metric dictionary directly. If the environment reuses that dictionary or updates its tensor buffers before the next log flush, earlier episode samples change as well. For successive reward samples `[1, 3]` and `[9, 9]`, the reported mean becomes 9 instead of 5.5. Mutable scalar entries in a reused dictionary are affected too.

## Change

Snapshot the selected `episode`/`log` mapping when collecting it and detach/clone its tensor values. Preserve the existing preference for `episode` when both keys are present. This keeps the stored samples independent of later environment mutations and avoids retaining their autograd graphs.

## Validation

- Reuse both dictionary and tensor buffers under each supported key; mutate them between collection calls and verify the eventual logged means, original snapshot, detached tensors and environment-owned values.
- Unchanged implementation: **2 failed, 4 passed** in the logger tests. Fixed independent branch: **272 passed, 6 skipped** in the local suite excluding the Gloo module.
- Combined fork integration with residual parameter normalization and collection fixes: **284 passed, 6 skipped** on Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12, including existing real two-process Gloo tests. Lint and Docs also pass. [Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43894272107).
- All repository pre-commit hooks pass.

Related: #267 changes aggregation at log flush. This patch fixes ownership at collection time; aggregation cannot recover samples that were already overwritten.

prs.title: Keep recurrent rollout collection outside autograd graphs
prs.head: d80408e5c32f54be094c366007767e0666de47bc
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

Direct use of `PPO.act()` or `Distillation.act()` outside the runner's `inference_mode` context records recurrent sampling graphs. Detaching returned actions does not detach the recurrent hidden state. In PPO, those graphs enter saved rollout states and a second learning epoch raises `Trying to backward through the graph a second time`. Distillation also keeps unnecessary teacher-state graphs during direct collection.

## Change

Run both public collection methods under `torch.no_grad()`, matching SAC collection and the runner's existing intended separation between sampling and learning. Gradient-enabled model calls in the update methods remain available for training.

## Validation

- GRU and LSTM direct PPO collection followed by two real learning epochs; verify finite losses, detached rollout states and changed model parameters.
- GRU and LSTM direct distillation collection followed by a real student update; verify detached teacher states and changed student parameters.
- Unchanged implementation: **4 failed, 43 passed** in the focused algorithm tests. Fixed independent branch: **274 passed, 6 skipped** in the local suite excluding the Gloo module.
- Combined fork integration with the normalization and metric-snapshot fixes: **284 passed, 6 skipped** on Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12, including existing real two-process Gloo tests. Lint and Docs also pass. [Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43894272107).
- All repository pre-commit hooks pass.

prs.title: Prevent finite gradients from overflowing during distributed averaging
prs.head: 7b3e479369be543774b97b0c54f964691f8b92f5
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

Gradient averaging currently sums each bucket in its original dtype and divides the result by the number of ranks. With float16 gradients, the intermediate sum can overflow even when every local gradient and the final average are finite. For example, local gradients of 30,000 and 40,000 become infinity during the two-rank sum, although their average is representable.

## Change

Divide each packed bucket or oversized gradient slice by `world_size` before the SUM reduction. This keeps the existing bucket size, gradient dtype, and communication layout while avoiding the world-size amplification of the intermediate sum. As with any change in floating-point operation order, the result can differ by rounding from sum-then-divide; this does not introduce a higher-precision communication buffer.

Add a real two-rank Gloo regression using a half-precision linear model, gradients produced by backward, and an SGD step. The test covers both packed buckets and oversized slices, checks the expected finite average, and verifies finite nonzero parameter updates.

## Validation

- Before the fix, the new distributed regressions fail in both bucket configurations: **2 failed, 275 passed, 6 skipped** on Python 3.9 ([run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43895146001)).
- After the fix, the complete test matrix passes on **Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12**; the Python 3.12 job reports **277 passed, 6 skipped**, including the real Gloo tests ([run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43896381391)).
- The existing distributed parameter-synchronization and unreduced-control tests pass.
- Pre-commit hooks, documentation, and lint checks pass.

prs.title: Preserve finite deterministic Beta actions across native and exported policies
prs.head: 322ca9909e97b6537f1540c953587640c5653156
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

The deterministic Beta policy computes `alpha / (alpha + beta)` in the network output dtype. The sum can overflow even when both concentrations and the bounded mean are finite. A half-precision policy with raw concentration outputs 40,000 and 30,000 consequently returns the lower action bound instead of an interior action near 0.14285 on the default [-1, 1] interval. Large finite float32 concentrations have the same failure.

The native policy, its cached distribution mean, and the deterministic export wrapper each contain this calculation.

## Change

Compute the ratio after scaling both concentrations by their maximum. This avoids an overflowing sum without forming a potentially overflowing `beta / alpha` ratio for highly asymmetric concentrations.

Share the deterministic-output calculation between native and exported policies. Evaluate float16/bfloat16 Softplus and mean arithmetic in float32, then restore the original output dtype. This also prevents the half-precision exported Softplus path from producing NaN for the finite large inputs in the regression.

## Validation

- New regressions fail on unchanged upstream: **3 failed, 280 passed, 6 skipped** in the full Python 3.9 test job ([before](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43897564719)).
- The complete fixed test matrix passes on **Python 3.9–3.12**, including the existing real Gloo tests ([after](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43898062514)).
- Regression coverage includes cached means, native deterministic actions, TorchScript, full half-precision MLP inference, and gradients into the model's output head.
- An additional actual ONNX Runtime CPU check passes for float16 and float32 policies and agrees with native and TorchScript results ([reproduction script](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/blob/afloat16/rsl-active-checkpoint-20261116/contribution-audit/rsl_beta_mean_probe.py), [results](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/blob/afloat16/rsl-active-checkpoint-20261116/contribution-audit/rsl-beta-mean-export-after.log)).
- Independent 100-digit Decimal mean and analytic-gradient checks cover highly asymmetric finite concentrations, including a representable float64 mean around `1.69e-308` and a nonzero gradient around `5e-309`.
- All repository pre-commit hooks, lint, and documentation checks pass.

No model parameters or checkpoint shapes change.

prs.title: Keep logging-only symmetry metrics from changing BatchNorm state
prs.head: 65e4f638fe2fe658cddbbdf0fba117b365f78eac
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

When symmetry is configured only for logging (`use_mirror_loss=False`), `Symmetry.compute_loss` still runs the actor in training mode. For a residual actor using BatchNorm, this diagnostic forward changes its running mean, running variance, and batch counter. Merely enabling the metric therefore changes the deployed policy and, in a seeded SAC reproduction, the critic updates.

Disabling autograd does not prevent this state change.

## Changes

Temporarily disable running-statistic tracking on the actor's BatchNorm modules during the logging-only forward, restoring each module's original setting in a `finally` block. The metric continues to use the same batch statistics and training mode. Symmetry used as a learned objective keeps its existing statistic updates and gradients.

The regression tests cover both data-augmentation settings, verify that learned symmetry still updates BatchNorm and differentiates through the actor, and compare real SAC rollout collection followed by two updates with and without logging-only symmetry. The actor state, critic state, and resulting deterministic actions agree exactly after this change.

## Validation

- Before the fix: **3 failed, 277 passed, 6 skipped** in the complete suite ([run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43900471443)).
- After the fix: **280 passed, 6 skipped** on each of Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12, including the real two-process Gloo tests ([run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43901493852)).
- [Lint](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43901493840) and [documentation](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43901493853) passed.
- The earlier logging-only autograd patch still fails all three new regressions when tested separately, confirming that this addresses a different state-management problem.

prs.title: Keep running observation moments finite and preserve float64 precision
prs.head: 56e6c903e5a48f57c14ac2aa4f94e3b691bd37b8
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

Finite observations can corrupt the running normalizer even when their mean and variance are representable:

- A constant float32 batch filled with `2e38`, or a float64 batch filled with `1e308`, overflows the separate mean reduction. The first calibration batch produces an infinite mean, a NaN standard deviation, and NaN policy outputs.
- Combining two batches can overflow the unweighted between-batch product before its sample weight is applied. For example, two float64 singleton batches `[0]` and `[2e154]` have a finite mean and standard deviation of `1e154`, but the running standard deviation becomes infinite.
- Dividing the integer sample counts produces a float32 update weight even for a double-precision normalizer. Updating with `[0]` and then `[1, 1]` stores `0.6666666865348816` instead of the float64 value of `2/3`.

## Changes

Compute the batch mean and variance together with `torch.var_mean`, form the sample weight using the normalizer buffer precision with a float32 minimum, and apply that weight before multiplying the between-batch mean differences. Running buffers retain their identity and checkpoint layout.

The tests exercise first-batch and repeated constant calibration, finite between-batch variance, unequal batch sizes, native MLP and TorchScript outputs, and backward propagation into the policy head.

## Validation

- Unchanged upstream with the new tests: **8 failed, 275 passed, 6 skipped** ([before](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43904392696)).
- Fixed complete suite: **283 passed, 6 skipped** on Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12 ([after](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43904909272)).
- The suite includes a real two-process Gloo comparison of repeated unequal per-rank batches against pooled float64 observations.
- Independent exact rational moments and 100-digit Decimal standard-deviation/output checks pass for seven scenarios, including first-batch `1e308` constants, opposite `±1e154` batch means, and pooled versus partitioned observations ([script](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/blob/afloat16/rsl-active-checkpoint-20261116/contribution-audit/rsl_normalization_moments_probe.py), [results](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/blob/afloat16/rsl-active-checkpoint-20261116/contribution-audit/rsl-normalization-decimal-after.json)).
- The earlier running-variance cancellation patch still fails all seven local regression cases when tested separately.
- [Lint](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43904909373), [documentation](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43904909334), and all repository pre-commit hooks passed.

The distributed communication protocol is unchanged. Extreme count-weighted collective sums remain subject to their existing range limits.

prs.title: Stop all distributed ranks on nonfinite environment data
prs.head: d9c2b4f4f75ea4cfcba946b5c1c05aaa8bf45e08
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

The runner checks for NaN and Inf after collecting a rollout, but the check is local to each rank. When only one environment shard returns invalid data, that rank raises `ValueError` while its healthy peers continue into the policy update. Their subsequent collectives no longer have matching participants, so the original environment failure can become a communication error or a stalled training run.

## Changes

- Add an opt-in synchronized failure check to `raise_if_nonfinite`. It reduces one integer flag per rollout, so different ranks can report different observation or final-observation keys without requiring identical flag dictionaries.
- Have distributed runners use that check when `check_for_nan` is enabled. All ranks raise before the policy update if any rank encountered invalid data; the failing rank retains the existing named-output error, and healthy peers identify a remote environment failure.
- Preserve the local utility default and the disabled-check path. Allocate the reduction flag outside inference mode so asynchronous process-group writes can safely update it.

## Validation

Two real CPU/Gloo processes first complete a healthy PPO training iteration. The regressions then inject either a NaN reward or an Inf final observation into only one rank and verify that both ranks report the failure, neither enters the next policy update, and actor parameters remain unchanged. The final-observation case also exercises unequal flag dictionaries across ranks.

- [Tests against the original implementation](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43906968787): **2 failed, 275 passed, 6 skipped**.
- [Tests with the fix](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43907704535): all Python **3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12** jobs passed; **277 passed, 6 skipped** in the recorded Python 3.12 job.
- [Lint](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43907704275) and [documentation](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43907704278) passed. Local `pre-commit run --all-files` passed.

The distributed execution above uses CPU/Gloo; the NCCL device-selection path was not exercised on GPU hardware.

prs.title: Preserve the direction of adaptive KL learning-rate changes
prs.head: 5a4811e3403b96085661ee99f575d0f8a58e8b6d
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

PPO's adaptive schedule can reverse its intended response when an explicitly configured or restored learning rate lies outside its usual bounds:

- With `learning_rate=1e-6`, a high KL changes the rate to `1e-5`: a tenfold **increase** in the branch intended to reduce the update size.
- With `learning_rate=0.02`, a small positive KL changes the rate to `0.01`: a **decrease** in the branch intended to increase it.

These values are applied to the actual optimizer before its step, so this affects model updates, not only the reported rate.

## Changes

Bound each adaptive adjustment by the current learning rate as well as the existing floor or ceiling. A high-KL adjustment can only lower or retain the rate; a low-KL adjustment can only raise or retain it. Rates within the existing `[1e-5, 1e-2]` range keep their current behavior. A rate outside that range is retained when the existing bound would otherwise reverse the adjustment; this does not add continued scaling beyond the bounds or a new configuration option.

## Validation

The regressions collect a real rollout, shift the Gaussian policy mean to produce a measured high or low KL, and run a complete PPO update. Actor and critic parameters are compared exactly with an independent fixed-rate PPO update using the expected rate. The cases cover both inversions and both ordinary in-range directions; existing tests retain the boundary-clamping cases.

- [Original implementation with the regressions](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43910781906): **2 failed, 277 passed, 6 skipped**.
- [Fixed complete suite](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43911365103): all Python **3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12** jobs passed; the recorded Python 3.12 job reports **279 passed, 6 skipped**.
- [Lint](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43911365120), [documentation](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43911365150), and local `pre-commit run --all-files` passed.

prs.title: Add optional pooled advantage normalization for distributed PPO
prs.head: e7ce3b26ae840f4535211ed859b7987daeaa21b3
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Closes #299.

## Purpose

This opt-in `extras` algorithm supports experiments that treat all distributed ranks as shards of one rollout. Standard PPO normalizes advantages independently on each rank; that remains a valid choice and its implementation and defaults are unchanged. `GlobalAdvantagePPO` instead uses the pooled rollout mean and sample standard deviation, preserving differences between rank-local advantage distributions.

## Implementation

- Select the subclass through the existing `algorithm.class_name` configuration. It reuses PPO's GAE, bootstrap-state handling and optimizer update.
- After computing returns, normalize raw `returns - values` with count-weighted pooled statistics. Two collectives carry three float64 scalar statistics (count, sum and centered squared deviation), without gathering rollout tensors.
- Keep single-process outputs and optimizer updates unchanged. Reject per-minibatch normalization because it would undo the requested pooled semantics.
- Document the feature, API and configuration on `extras`. Unequal shards receive correctly weighted statistics, but matching a pooled optimizer update requires equal-sized rank-local batches because PPO averages gradients equally across ranks. Multiple minibatches also require corresponding sample groupings.

This adds an algorithm choice, not a convergence or throughput claim. Local normalization may be preferable for heterogeneous tasks or reward scales.

## Validation

Actual two-process CPU/Gloo tests collect a rollout and compare the normalized advantages, actor/critic gradients and complete Adam parameter update with a single-process PPO trained on the combined rollout. The update checks use `rtol=2e-5, atol=2e-6`; a separate core-PPO control confirms that local normalization has different advantages and actor updates. Singleton shards, unequal sample counts, constant advantages, inference-mode collection, configuration construction and incompatible settings are covered.

- [Local-normalization ablation](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43913808535): **2 failed, 278 passed**. This intentionally leaves the new subclass delegating to core PPO, and the pooled-equivalence/statistics tests detect the missing feature.
- [Complete implementation](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43914324924): **all Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12 jobs passed**; the recorded Python 3.12 job reports **280 passed**.
- [Lint](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43914324927), [documentation](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43914324922), local non-distributed suite (**272 passed**) and `pre-commit run --all-files` passed.

The distributed execution evidence is CPU/Gloo; GPU/NCCL execution has not been measured here.

prs.title: Add optional dynamic batch size to ONNX policy export
prs.head: 6286856b5c784d439dc039a692d696f54cccdb4e
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Use case

Batched policy evaluation currently needs custom ONNX export code, including different batch axes for recurrent states. This adds the opt-in `dynamic_batch=False` argument to the existing `OnPolicyRunner.export_policy_to_onnx` method, as proposed in #301.

## Changes

- With `dynamic_batch=True`, observation/image/action tensors use batch axis 0; GRU/LSTM hidden and cell tensors use axis 1. All share the `batch` symbol, while feature dimensions, image dimensions and recurrent layer/hidden dimensions stay fixed.
- The optional path explicitly selects `dynamo=False` and dynamic axes, reusing the current model wrappers. It has no exporter retry or version-dependent fallback.
- Omitting the argument preserves the existing fixed-batch export and exporter selection. The guide describes batched use and recurrent-state feedback.

The legacy route is deliberate: the modern exporter in PyTorch 2.6 fails on the tested dynamic LSTM with `Cannot call numel() on tensor with symbolic sizes/strides`. Current PyTorch deprecates the legacy exporter, so this limitation is documented. Deployment-runtime compatibility and throughput are outside the validation performed here.

## Validation

The public runner export method is exercised with MLP, CNN, two-layer GRU and two-layer LSTM policies. ONNX checker and strict shape inference verify static non-batch dimensions and the shared dynamic symbol. ONNX's local `ReferenceEvaluator` matches native actions and recurrent states at batch sizes 1, 3 and 7. Recurrent tests feed each exported state output into a second inference step. Default fixed-batch exports are also checked.

- Focused shape/numerical tests: 16 passed on PyTorch 2.6.0 and 16 passed on 2.15.0 (Python 3.12, ONNX 1.23.2).
- Local suite on PyTorch 2.6.0: 285 passed; pre-commit checks passed. Native Gloo tests run in remote CI.
- Feature ablation (the option accepted but dynamic axes disabled): [8 expected failures, 281 passes and 1 evaluator skip](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43917474967).
- Complete implementation: [all four Python 3.9–3.12 jobs passed](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43917724434); Python 3.12 ran 290 tests, and Python 3.9 ran 288 with 2 explicitly skipped LSTM numerical cases. The older ONNX reference evaluator omits the cell-state output; LSTM checker/shape tests still run there. Lint and documentation checks passed.

Closes #301. This extends the existing ONNX exporter; it is separate from the additional export format discussed in #269.

prs.title: Fix Minkowski sum seeds for translated and disconnected operands
prs.head: edfefbd03da6fe87f94f0553906fee32b69159bb
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #1968.

`MinkowskiSum` currently unions its face/vertex sweeps with the unshifted first operand. That solid need not belong to the sum when the other operand does not contain the origin. Two unit cubes, with the second translated by `(10, 0, 0)`, produce volume **9 instead of 8** and retain an unrelated cube at the origin. For disconnected operands of different sizes, the boundary sweeps also leave contained interiors unfilled: the two-by-two box example in the issue gives **610 instead of 864**, with both missing and excess geometry.

This change fixes the interior seeds used by the existing sum construction:

- Convex/convex sums use their complete vertex-sum hull directly.
- Non-convex/convex sums seed the result with the first solid translated by an actual vertex of the second.
- Non-convex/non-convex sums seed both directions at a vertex of every boundary component. The existing union-find helper finds those components, including cavity surfaces. Every seed has the form `A + b` or `B + a`, so it belongs to the mathematical sum; seeds fill containment regions that face-pair sweeps alone miss.

The existing difference construction keeps its original base and paths. The public API and the final cancellation/error/original-ID handling are unchanged.

## Validation

- New native C++ regression: **24 operand/translation combinations**, each evaluated in both orders. Inputs cover convex cubes, L shapes, disconnected components of unequal sizes, a frame, a closed cavity, and a separate solid nested inside that cavity. Translations include negative coordinates and remain lazy when passed to `MinkowskiSum`.
- Expected results are independently built by distributing the sum over unions of axis-aligned boxes. Checks require **both Boolean differences to be empty**, in addition to status/volume checks, and verify the inputs retain their geometry.
- The new regression fails against the unchanged upstream library and passes with this change.
- All **10** focused native tests pass, covering the new regression, existing sum/difference cases, cancellation, error propagation, and constructor original IDs. Repeated with GCC 14.2, `MANIFOLD_PAR=OFF`, and `MANIFOLD_STRICT=ON`, `MANIFOLD_DEBUG=ON`, `MANIFOLD_ASSERT=ON`.
- Clang-format 20 and `git diff --check` pass.

The strict focused run uses the current base `74493803`; the original release baseline at `9ebbfb51` also passed its complete **640-test** native suite. Cross-platform/TBB checks are left to the repository CI.

prs.title: Preserve operand order when computing Minkowski differences
prs.head: 2da50113cf9ce19976748ff02ec71a51501282ab
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #1970.

Eroding a convex first operand by a non-convex second operand currently runs the operation in the opposite direction. `Impl::Minkowski` uses a convex-first swap for both sums and differences, even though a difference is not commutative. For a `10 × 10 × 10` box and the centered symmetric cross in the issue, the result is empty instead of the expected `6 × 6 × 9` box (volume **324**).

This change limits the swap to sums and routes erosion of a convex first operand through the existing per-face/all-cutter-vertices hull path. For convex A, `A ⊖ B = A ⊖ conv(B)`, so this path also handles a non-convex cutter without the face-pair sweep's enclosing-cutter gap. The original first operand remains the erosion base. No public parameter is introduced.

## Validation

- A native regression uses a non-convex symmetric cross, both 0° and 90° rotations, and centered/translated first operands. The reference is an analytic axis-aligned box; both `expected - result` and `result - expected` must be empty. The reversed operation is also checked and remains empty.
- The regression fails against unchanged upstream and passes with this change. Following review, it also covers the larger cross completely eroding a small convex box, including rotation and negative translation. Those four empty-result assertions fail against the initial version of this PR and pass after the routing correction.
- A rotated, translated tetrahedron is eroded by the cross and by its convex hull; both directional set differences between the results are empty.
- All **10** focused native tests pass with GCC 14.2, `MANIFOLD_PAR=OFF`, and `MANIFOLD_STRICT=ON`, `MANIFOLD_DEBUG=ON`, `MANIFOLD_ASSERT=ON`. This includes all existing Minkowski sum/difference cases, cancellation, error propagation, and original-ID checks.
- The original Python-binding reproducer returns volume **324**, with zero missing or excess volume; reversing its operands remains empty.
- Clang-format 20 and `git diff --check` pass.

This patch is independently based on `74493803` and does not include or depend on the sum-seeding change in #1969. The separate non-convex-base and empty-base cases reported in #1980 are outside this convex-base fix.

prs.title: Elide redundant MeshGL copies in C exports
prs.head: c09c5b3b28a7e880f17e2ca644d78a81972f493d
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

The four C mesh-export functions first save the C++ value result in a local `mesh`, then copy that lvalue into the heap-owned `MeshGL` or `MeshGL64`. This deep-copies every nonempty mesh buffer just before the temporary buffers are destroyed. Large exports therefore pay for a second full payload allocation and copy.

## Change

Directly initialize the returned heap object from the C++ export value in:

- `manifold_get_meshgl`
- `manifold_get_meshgl_w_normals`
- `manifold_get_meshgl64`
- `manifold_get_meshgl64_w_normals`

The project already requires C++17, so the prvalue initializes the destination directly. The C API and its independent-buffer ownership remain unchanged.

## Validation

- Strict native Release build with `MANIFOLD_DEBUG=ON`, `MANIFOLD_ASSERT=ON`, and `MANIFOLD_PAR=OFF`: all **25 CBIND tests pass**.
- A native benchmark calls all four public C exports and compares every mesh field with the corresponding C++ value export. All four exported meshes remain valid after deleting the source Manifold.
- For a sphere with 524,288 triangles, 262,146 vertices and six position/normal properties, requested C++ allocation bytes during one export are:

| Export | Before | After | Removed allocation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32-bit, default or explicit normals | 36,700,758 | 24,117,785 | 12,582,973 bytes |
| 64-bit, default or explicit normals | 61,866,698 | 36,700,757 | 25,165,941 bytes |

The reduction is exactly one full mesh-buffer payload (about 12 MiB / 24 MiB). A second mesh size and repeated runs give the same relationship. These figures measure requested allocation bytes, not process RSS; no general latency claim is needed for the change.

[Reproducible benchmark, build commands, raw measurements and native test log](https://github.com/Afloat16/manifold/tree/c7efbb2245fb592702ce7cadbb76ee274a881419/contribution-validation/capi-export-copy).

Changed lines also pass clang-format 20.1.8 and `git diff --check`.

prs.title: Keep exported tangents aligned with sorted triangle runs
prs.head: 7956d427fe0efa3d02bfa1ef0354477b11ffcf40
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #1973

## Problem

`GetMeshGLImpl` sorts triangles into their original-mesh runs, but copies `halfedgeTangent` in the internal triangle order. A valid smoothed composite can therefore export tangents attached to the wrong halfedges. Re-importing the mesh and calling `Refine` can return `InvalidTangents`.

For two disjoint smoothed spheres, with the first scaled by `(1, 2, 3)` and translated, direct `Refine(3)` succeeds with volume `28.811953597006113`; the exported/re-imported version previously failed and returned an empty error result.

## Change

Copy the four tangent components alongside each exported triangle corner, using the same `oldTri` permutation as `triVerts`. The template covers both `MeshGL` and `MeshGL64`. Meshes without tangent data keep the existing path.

## Validation

- The new native `Smooth.ExportTangentsFollowTriangleRuns` regression fails on the unchanged base and passes with the fix.
- All **22 native Smooth tests pass** in a strict Release build with debug checks and assertions enabled.
- Six scenarios in both precisions cover single meshes, transformed meshes, both component orders, different originals, and mixed smooth/faceted components.
- The regression checks successful import/refinement, triangle counts, volume and surface area, plus both Boolean differences against direct refinement.
- In the independent native Python-binding reproduction, all six 64-bit round trips have zero excess and missing volume. The 32-bit differences remain below `2.2e-6`, consistent with export rounding.
- clang-format 20.1.8 and `git diff --check` pass.

prs.title: Store exported property-vertex bins in contiguous arrays
prs.head: 2009ea8c75d844569faeb07caacddc5586b90f89
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

Every MeshGL export with vertex properties creates a separate `std::vector` bin for each geometric vertex. Even a smooth mesh with one property vertex per geometric vertex performs one small allocation per vertex, in addition to the output arrays.

## Change

Store the property bins in contiguous arrays: one head index per geometric vertex, and one `{property, next}` entry per output vertex. The output vertex index is the entry index. This keeps the existing first-encounter vertex numbering, merge destinations, properties and run metadata while avoiding the individual bin allocations. The no-properties path is unchanged. Both MeshGL precisions use the same implementation.

## Validation

- **644 native tests pass** with GCC 14.2, Release, strict mode, debug checks and assertions enabled. An interrupted run was resumed for the remaining registered tests on the same binary; no tests were excluded.
- **40 full exports are byte-for-byte identical** before and after, totaling 127,248,646 bytes. These cover 32/64-bit output and explicit normal indices; no properties, smooth/faceted normals, property seams, booleans, tangents, many properties, constant properties, mixed-normal runs, transforms and empty meshes. Every public MeshGL field is included in the comparison.
- Native allocation counters for representative meshes:

| Export | Allocations before → after | Requested allocation bytes before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Smooth sphere, 524,288 triangles, MeshGL | 262,156 → 11 | 24,117,537 → 18,874,617 |
| Same sphere, MeshGL64 | 262,156 → 11 | 36,700,509 → 31,457,589 |
| Faceted sphere, 32,768 triangles, MeshGL | 65,584 → 47 | 7,405,641 → 5,898,417 |
| Same faceted sphere, MeshGL64 | 65,584 → 47 | 12,255,309 → 10,748,085 |

The unchanged no-properties control still performs 8 allocations in both precisions. These counters measure requested C++ allocations during one public export, not process RSS. Shared-host timings were noisy, so no latency claim is made.

[Native benchmark, complete results and test logs](https://github.com/Afloat16/manifold/tree/validation/export-property-bins-20261116/contribution-validation/export-property-bins).

clang-format 20.1.8 and `git diff --check` pass.

prs.title: Preserve non-finite errors from warp callbacks
prs.head: 27a6591e0d36272183ef5599862fd96b1d078622
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
Fixes #1977

## Problem

A warp callback can produce non-finite coordinates yet return an empty manifold with `Error::NoError`. `CalculateBBox()` clears a mesh whose bounds are non-finite, so the subsequent `IsFinite()` check sees an empty vertex array and cannot report the callback error.

## Change

Run the existing finite-vertex check immediately after the callback, before calculating bounds. Invalid callback results retain `Error::NonFiniteVertex`; the normal bounds, sorting and normal calculations keep their existing order for finite results.

## Validation

- The new native regression fails on the original code and passes with this change. It checks positive infinity, negative infinity and NaN on all three axes through `Warp`, a single-vertex `WarpBatch`, and an all-vertex `WarpBatch` (27 error-status checks).
- The same regression checks a valid volume-changing warp, unchanged source geometry and an empty input.
- All **103 native `Manifold.*` tests pass** with GCC 14.2, Release, strict mode, debug checks and assertions enabled.
- clang-format 20.1.8 and `git diff --check` pass.

prs.title: Share topology buffers when copy-constructing SharedVec
prs.head: f7928a234891089683ea41b65a4f8b4bd0d98f43
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

`SharedVec` documents that copy construction shares its storage, but its copy constructor currently constructs a new vector from the source view. Topology-preserving operations that copy `Impl` therefore allocate and copy all three halfedge arrays even though they never modify them.

## Change

Use the existing shared copy-assignment behavior when copy-constructing a `SharedVec`. Keep the explicit `MakeUnique()` mutation contract and deep-copy behavior when copying to an ordinary unshared `Vec`.

Both shared-to-unshared move paths also detach before transferring storage. Without that step, making copy construction share would allow an unshared vector to own a buffer that another shared vector still uses. Copying and copy-assigning a moved-from empty vector remain supported. A null source counter creates a fresh empty vector before releasing the destination; regressions cover empty, unique and shared destinations and their subsequent reuse. The throwing-callback test remains enabled for native builds and is excluded from Emscripten builds without exception catching.

## Current-head validation

At `f7928a234891089683ea41b65a4f8b4bd0d98f43`:

- Native strict/debug/assert build: **6 focused SharedVec/topology tests passed**, including throwing callbacks and concurrent copies.
- Actual Emscripten 5.0.2 build: **3 focused tests passed**, and the throwing-callback test is excluded. The old guard was reproduced aborting on the same toolchain.
- The moved-from copy-assignment reproducer changes from a null-counter ASan/UBSan failure to a clean exit. LeakSanitizer remains disabled in the local traced environment.
- clang-format 20.1.8 and `git diff --check`: passed.
- [Upstream CI](https://github.com/elalish/manifold/actions/runs/44003802416) and [TSAN](https://github.com/elalish/manifold/actions/runs/44003802422) have passed for this head. All **45 checks are successful**, including WASM/nix-js, ASan/UBSan, TSAN, the performance guard, cross-platform determinism and [formatting](https://github.com/elalish/manifold/actions/runs/44003802419).

## Initial implementation validation

The following full-suite and performance results were recorded at the preceding head `b6ab77889b996ed19348e58ea6c26684f58bf740`:

- **649 native tests pass** in Release with strict mode, debug checks and assertions enabled.
- **660 tests pass in the repository's configured ThreadSanitizer suite** with GCC 14 and instrumented TBB, including the new concurrent copy/detach and public topology-copy cases: [independent fork run](https://github.com/Afloat16/manifold/actions/runs/43936963443).
- Added regressions cover shared storage, explicit detach, both shared-to-unshared move paths, empty/moved-from sources, public topology mutations, throwing callbacks, and concurrent copies. All public mesh fields of the source remain unchanged after mutations of a copy.
- Header-level ownership regressions fail on the base and pass under ASan/UBSan after the change. LeakSanitizer was disabled because it cannot run under the local traced environment; no leak-check result is claimed.
- **Seven complete MeshGL64 payloads are byte-for-byte identical** before and after (56,624,539 bytes), including original geometry before and after the operations.

For a native sphere with 65,538 vertices and 131,072 triangles, allocation counters during each public operation measured:

| Operation | Allocations before → after | Requested allocation bytes before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| SetProperties | 20 → 14 | 31,458,360 → 26,739,756 |
| CalculateCurvature | 25 → 19 | 35,718,330 → 30,999,726 |
| SmoothByNormals | 196,640 → 196,634 | 196,636,050 → 191,917,446 |

Each avoids six allocations and 4,718,604 requested bytes. A normal-changing operation that must detach and an ordinary lazy copy retain their original allocation counts and bytes. These are requested allocations, not process RSS or a latency claim.

[Native benchmark, complete results and consumer audit](https://github.com/Afloat16/manifold/tree/validation/sharedvec-copy-sharing-20261116/contribution-validation/sharedvec-copy-sharing).

clang-format 20.1.8 and `git diff --check` pass.

prs.title: Skip unrequested curvature channels
prs.head: 395023a8a3f6442cf87bb2dceea4fc8e61f9b266
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Problem

`CalculateCurvature` accepts a negative channel index to leave that result unstored, and mean-only calls are used by the smoothing examples/tests. The implementation still allocates both curvature buffers and calculates both results for every triangle.

## Changes

Allocate and accumulate only the requested curvature channels. Skip the mean-curvature dihedral calculation when the mean channel is negative, and skip the Gaussian corner-angle calculation when the Gaussian channel is negative. Keep the shared area/degree calculation and the final property-channel writes unchanged.

Add coverage for mean-only and Gaussian-only requests on smooth, faceted, and concave inputs, both overwriting existing channels and extending the property set. The test also checks preserved channels and input immutability.

## Validation

- All 36 selected native tests pass (`Properties.*`, `Smooth.*`, and the curvature error-propagation test), using GCC 14.2, Release, assertions/debug checks enabled, and `MANIFOLD_PAR=OFF`.
- Twelve public-API cases cover single channels, both channels, aliased channels, neither channel, existing properties, concave/faceted meshes, and an empty input. All 11 public MeshGL64 fields match the baseline byte for byte. Including before/after input snapshots, 16 serialized payloads totaling 37,635,779 bytes match.
- On a 65,538-vertex / 131,072-triangle sphere, a single-channel request drops from 23 allocations / 30,475,290 requested bytes to 22 allocations / 29,950,986 bytes. The omitted buffer is exactly `8 * NumVert()` = 524,304 bytes.
- Requests for both channels and neither channel have unchanged allocation counts and requested bytes.
- Clang-format 20 and `git diff --check` pass.

The benchmark records allocation requests during the actual public operation. Timing samples varied across runs, so this change makes no elapsed-time improvement claim. Source, raw results, full-field hashes, and native-test logs are in [the validation record](https://github.com/Afloat16/manifold/tree/validation/curvature-requested-channels-20261116/contribution-validation/curvature-requested-channels).

prs.title: perf(firmware): bound retained diagnostic descriptions
prs.head: dd42eb715349651889b4b49c1be9ce0362454070
prs.author: Afloat16
prs.body:
## Summary

Reduce temporary diagnostic allocations when inspecting large UF2 and DfuSe files. The decoders now construct only the four descriptions that their existing summaries display, while counting every omitted description. All payload regions, metadata, coverage, integrity facts and summary wording remain unchanged.

## Problem and expected behavior

At base `d5a942177fad030d3caf0f8d39856c116e3e5cda`, `overlappingElements` formats a string for each nonempty overlapping DfuSe element; `numberingFacts` similarly retains every absent or ambiguous UF2 numbering-group description. Their consumers later display only four examples. Thus an admitted file can allocate tens of thousands of strings that are immediately discarded.

Related: #8230 / `1f935949ff904165f90b4740eb283a8218275a13` bounded descriptions for **empty** DfuSe declarations during the target walk. This change covers retained nonempty payload overlaps and UF2 numbering groups, which that patch and its review discussion left unchanged. #11296 centralized summary formatting with `boundedList`; it did not bound these producers. No separate issue is linked because the reproduction, measurements and proposed repair are included here.

## Change and scope

The two domain producers return `BoundedList<string>` with explicit omitted counts. They still examine every element/group; only descriptions beyond the displayed four are avoided. UF2 formats group labels only when a retained description needs them. The existing consumers use the bounded owner for both wording and total counts. Both formats are included as one diagnostic-retention improvement.

## Contract and boundary impact

- Semantic owners: DfuSe overlap reporting and UF2 numbering facts; their artifact readers and CLI/MCP consumers retain the same facts.
- Contribution scope: ordinary optimization of existing local-file parsers; no advance scope decision required.
- CLI/MCP, provider and format compatibility: no input, output schema, ceiling or admission change.
- Evidence/provenance: entry identity, source ranges, payload bytes, coverage and integrity remain intact.
- Target authority and cleanup: unchanged file reads and existing reader lifetime.
- Generated metadata, packaging and installation: no changes.

Expected effects:

- [x] Read existing files or captured data.
- [ ] Launch or attach to a process.
- [ ] Inject instrumentation or run scripts/code.
- [ ] Change process memory, registers, files, or configuration.
- [ ] Contact network services.
- [ ] Recover protected code or work around protections.
- [ ] Documentation or usability only; no target interaction.
- [ ] Not sure yet; investigation or maintainer guidance needed.

## Evidence and regression coverage

- DfuSe regression retains the full element list and payloads while checking address-order descriptions, total overlap count, different alternate settings and the exact omitted count.
- UF2 regression combines nine groups with absent and ambiguous numbering, checks the two summaries in encounter order, every region's source block indices and all payload bytes, plus a complete group.
- These are semantic-preservation tests and pass on both implementations. The allocation change is established separately by native measurements, not by a claimed failing functional regression.

Measured using fresh Node 24.22.1 processes on Ubuntu 24.04, three alternating before/after rounds. Peak RSS includes the whole process through complete enumeration and JSON serialization. The public-reader tasks enumerate every entry; small tasks also open every payload stream. Large decoder tasks independently verify every payload byte. Full outputs are compared byte-for-byte.

| Completed public-reader task | Input | Peak RSS before | Peak RSS after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DfuSe, 65,536 nonempty overlapping elements | 786,733 bytes | 397,800 KiB | 360,460 KiB |
| UF2, 21,845 ambiguous numbering groups | 33,553,920 bytes | 282,844 KiB | 270,560 KiB |
| UF2, 65,536 absent-number groups | 33,554,432 bytes | 456,108 KiB | 456,260 KiB |
| UF2, 8,192 complete groups (control) | 8,388,608 bytes | 182,876 KiB | 185,832 KiB |

The first two tasks save median 36.46 MiB and 12.00 MiB respectively. The absence-only public task is essentially unchanged; the complete-group control increases by 2.89 MiB. Decoder-only peaks and all individual measurements are retained with the logs. Full output sizes are unchanged, including the 29,515,333-byte DfuSe inventory and 9,823,589-byte ambiguous UF2 inventory.

Small and non-overlapping cases show no meaningful memory improvement. These synthetic cases establish the reported memory effect; they do not establish a general CPU, latency or token reduction. No hardware flashing or third-party firmware corpus was used.

For evidence-bearing changes:

- [x] Observed, derived, and inferred claims remain distinguishable.
- [x] Artifact identity, source provenance, and failed attempts remain preserved.
- [x] Unsupported, incomplete, unavailable, or uncertain outcomes remain visible.

## Validation performed

At the pinned base plus the exact four files in this PR:

- `npm run test:local -- src/domain/firmware/dfuse.test.ts src/artifacts/DfuSeArtifactReader.test.ts src/domain/firmware/uf2.test.ts src/artifacts/Uf2ArtifactReader.test.ts` — **45 passed before and after**.
- `npm run test:focused -- tests/acceptance/firmwareContainersCli.test.ts tests/boundary/mcp/firmwareContainersMcp.test.ts` — **7 passed** with the combined change; the same seven passed on the baseline in the earlier run.
- `npm run check` — **passed**, including typecheck, lint, formatting, Knip, metadata and architecture checks; existing typed-lint advisory warnings remain.
- `git diff --check` — passed; the only source-worktree changes are the four PR files.
- **96 fresh native processes** across the DfuSe and UF2 probes: all completed, every full before/after output matched byte-for-byte. Independent assertions checked counts, ordering, addresses, coverage and payloads.
- [DfuSe native/public validation and original comparison](https://github.com/Afloat16/rea/actions/runs/44032525389) and [combined exact-file validation, UF2 public measurements and full-history audit](https://github.com/Afloat16/rea/actions/runs/44034092158) — successful. The latter records SHA-256 for all four tested files; production readback matches those bytes.

The earlier validation workflow initially failed to start because of a job-level context expression; the corrected workflow completed. No failed or interrupted run is counted as a pass.

## Compatibility, safety, and release

No breaking change, migration, dependency or package change. Validation covers native Node/Linux parsers, the production ArtifactReader APIs, and the compiled CLI/MCP firmware tests; no Hopper/Ghidra or browser provider is involved. Existing parser and reader regressions remain in the selected suites. No new execution or mutation capability is introduced.
